544495|2026-03.headline: NIS Management Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 13.96% to INR180.03 crore; FY26 PAT hit by INR27.82 crore labour-code provision, adjusted PAT INR19.12 crore.
544495|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income was INR180.03 crore (up 13.96% YoY), with EBITDA of INR11.11 crore (up 29.75%) and margin of 9.41% (up 115 bps). FY26 consolidated income was INR436.70 crore (up 7.74%) and EBITDA INR33.53 crore (up 12.19%, margin 7.68%, up 30 bps). Reported profitability absorbed a one-time, non-cash exceptional provision of INR27.82 crore for the new Labour Codes; adjusted FY26 PAT was INR19.12 crore and adjusted Q4 PAT INR6.86 crore. Management guided to 12-15% consolidated growth and a target of crossing INR500 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Security services
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at INR199.49 crore, 46.03% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Housekeeping and payroll
segments.commentary: INR171.01 crore, 39.46% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Integrated FM, electronic security and CCTV rentals
segments.commentary: INR56.91 crore, 13.31% of revenue. CCTV was about INR12 crore, of which about INR7 crore was rental, generating roughly INR4 crore EBITDA.

segments.name: Other (course fees, allied receipts)
segments.commentary: INR5.99 crore in FY26. Keertika Academy revenue fell from about INR4 crore to INR2 crore as DDU-GKY projects ended; Education Associates LLP flat at about INR4 crore.

segments.name: NIS Facility Management Services (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell from about INR20 crore to INR16 crore as low-margin housing-society security contracts were exited. Standalone NIS Management grew about 10%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 12-15%, based on current order book plus in-year wins.
Management targets crossing INR500 crore consolidated revenue within FY26-27 timeframe (per call; target stated as 'within this financial year') and sees possible upside.
Expects CCTV revenue to pick up toward year end, with tenders in the next 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work; AMC contracts expected to add margin.
Expects DDU-GKY Odisha project by June; Maharashtra and West Bengal DDU-GKY bids still under evaluation.
Plans to deploy the unutilised IPO proceeds (INR36.91 crore unutilised) significantly this year and fully within two years.
Management said it will not pursue growth that would compromise operating cash flow or margins.
capex_capacity: Operates across 14 states via 14 branches, 18,000+ personnel and more than 1,500 client sites.
CCTV revenue was flat in FY26 due to STQC Make-in-India certification, causing camera stock-outs.

New contracts: Haldia Dock (about INR50 lakh per month, three years), Reliance Gujarat (about 150 stores, about INR1 crore), Patna Secretariat (about INR1 crore per year for three years), West Bengal Irrigation Department (about INR1 crore for one year), NBDD (about INR10 lakh billing).
HDFC Bank branch additions, plus IndusInd and ICICI Bank additions in North India, add about INR10 crore per month in total.
Government CCTV work: Webel/New Town Smart City (INR56 lakh), Mumbai Police CCTV project (INR1 crore), Patna Secretariat housekeeping (INR10.36 crore over five years).
demand_pricing: Management expects West Bengal government tenders to lift business after the change in government; 2-3 more work orders expected from New Town Smart City and the electricity board.
Security market growing about 10-11% YoY; company says it is growing at 12-13%.
Labour-code wage pass-through: all contract labour costs, minimum wage hikes, PF, ESIC, leave and gratuity are passed through to clients, with no renegotiation demands yet.
West Bengal accounts for about 70-75% of business; draft labour-code rules from the state government are still awaited.
Largest clients: Reliance Retail about INR30 crore (INR35-36 crore expected FY27), DTET about INR24 crore, airport INR22-23 crore, HDFC Bank about INR19 crore, Anjali Jewellers INR12-13 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue growth muted, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone grew about 10% as major contracts came in H2 (Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat) with little time to convert. Subsidiary revenue fell due to CCTV stock-outs, exits from low-margin housing-society contracts and delayed West Bengal projects; Keertika Academy fell about INR2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade receivables high at about INR145 crore and what is the aging?
qa_highlights.answer: NIS Management debtors rose from INR107 crore (H1 start) to INR119 crore in H1 and INR124 crore by year-end, due to collection delays at Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat, Patna Secretariat and Irrigation. Debtors were about INR120 crore in April after collections; over 180 days is about INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Bengal election changed renewals, payments or tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact on wins: a New Secretariat renewal came from PWD and a Webel CCTV order was won. DTET payments were delayed for April and May due to vote-on-account funding, though April was collected.

qa_highlights.question: Is there FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided 12-15% consolidated growth from the order book plus in-year wins. The MD cited a target of over INR500 crore in FY27 against INR436 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much annual revenue was lost from contracts ended or not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 revenue was about INR373 crore against INR352 crore in FY24 standalone, as Calcutta Airport (about INR15 crore a year) and IIT Bhubaneswar (INR6-7 crore) were lost. No renewals fell due in FY26; Calcutta Airport re-bid is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the labour-code impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract labour costs are passed through to clients, and no client has sought renegotiation yet. Formalisation may cut informal operators' margins while expanding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not 30-40% given the small base?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said faster growth is possible but low-margin, extended-credit tenders would hurt margins, cash flow and DSO. The company wants margins from most contracts before accelerating.

qa_highlights.question: Why are IPO proceeds not fully deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: INR36.91 crore is unutilised. New contracts started only from November to January after the September IPO, and about INR10 crore was deployed and recovered, so full deployment is expected within two years.

qa_highlights.question: When will CCTV revenue rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better CCTV returns toward year end, with tenders in 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work, plus AMC contracts for higher margin within about six months.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR145 crore (about 33% of FY26 revenue) and collection delays from government clients such as DTET and Haldia Dock.
Pending West Bengal draft labour-code rules, which could affect wage and compliance costs for the 70-75% of business in that state.
EBITDA margin mix risk: security and housekeeping run at about 4.5-4.8% EBITDA, while higher-margin CCTV and IFM are stagnant.
Keertika Academy and DDU-GKY tenders for Maharashtra and West Bengal remain under evaluation.
Calcutta Airport re-bid and government renewals (New Secretariat, Nabanna) due next year.
Deployment of INR36.91 crore unutilised IPO proceeds.
544495|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the West Bengal government pipeline and on CCTV recovery, but cautious on growth pace, citing margin and cash-flow discipline. Answers on receivables and the IPO were detailed, and some were hard to follow; the CFO and MD were occasionally evasive on FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: So we are slightly shy of really increasing revenue without a very strong consideration towards the bottom line either in the terms of the margin or even the cash flow.
And we would not want a situation where our operating cash flow, especially free cash flow, going below what it is today.
This impact i s non -cash, accounting -led and transitionary in nature, reflecting alignment with statutory obligations.
So we should be crossing INR500 crores within this financial year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose 115 bps to 9.41% and FY26 margin 7.68% (+30 bps), with CCTV and AMC (higher margin) expected to add margin toward year end, but security and housekeeping run at about 4.5-4.8% EBITDA and management is prioritising margin over growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No owned capacity expansion was detailed; growth is from service contracts across 14 branches and 18,000+ personnel, and CCTV revenue was flat in FY26 due to STQC certification stock-outs.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 12-15% consolidated FY27 revenue growth (midpoint 13.5%) on the current order book plus in-year wins, and says security market grows about 10-11% while the company is growing 12-13%; standalone grew about 10% in FY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the company is service-led with no utilisation metric given, and IPO proceeds of INR36.91 crore unutilised are to be deployed into operations rather than new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management sees possible upside to the INR500 crore FY27 target (vs INR436.70 crore in FY26, a 14.5% gap) if West Bengal tenders and 2-3 New Town Smart City and electricity board work orders convert.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables of about INR145 crore (about 33% of FY26 revenue) with collection delays from DTET and Haldia Dock, DTET payments delayed in April-May on vote-on-account funding, and pending West Bengal draft labour-code rules for 70-75% of business.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CCTV recovery depends on STQC certification and camera supply with tenders expected in 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work; AMC contracts expected within about six months; no new product launch named.

rows.label: West Bengal government pipeline and DDU-GKY Odisha project
rows.why: Management expects West Bengal tenders to lift business after the government change, with 2-3 more work orders from New Town Smart City and the electricity board, and DDU-GKY Odisha expected by June; Maharashtra and West Bengal DDU-GKY bids still under evaluation.

rows.label: Receivables collection of about INR145 crore
rows.why: Debtors rose from INR107 crore to INR124 crore by year-end (about 33% of FY26 revenue), with about INR5 crore over 180 days; management says it will not pursue growth that compromises cash flow, so collection improvement is expected only gradually.

rows.label: Deploy INR36.91 crore unutilised IPO proceeds
rows.when: significantly this year, fully within two years
rows.why: INR36.91 crore is unutilised after the September IPO, and about INR10 crore was deployed and recovered, so management plans significant deployment this year.

tone.note: Management was confident on the West Bengal government pipeline and CCTV recovery but cautious on growth pace, citing margin and cash-flow discipline; analysts probed receivables, IPO deployment and FY27 guidance, where the CFO and MD were occasionally evasive.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.
544495|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, and EBITDA rose 36.24% to INR9.22 crore with margin up 121 bps to 7.99%. Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.

segments.name: Security and manpower (standalone)
segments.commentary: Security revenue INR54.98 crore and housekeeping INR41.88 crore in June 2026 quarter; management cites ~9.95% EBITDA for manpower-type businesses (security, housekeeping, payroll).

segments.name: IFM and payroll
segments.commentary: IFM revenue INR10.28 crore and payroll services INR3.40 crore in the quarter; management says manpower businesses have similar profitability.

segments.name: CCTV and electronic security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.11 crore with a loss at PAT level in Q1, attributed to project execution costs ahead of bill raising; management expects stabilisation by September quarter and calls it the most profitable segment. FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore.

segments.name: Vocational training (LLP and Keertika Academy)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue nil (INR0 lakh); net loss about INR57 lakh across the LLP and Keertika Academy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target: cross INR500 crore consolidated, with management saying FY26 Nov-Dec onwards revenues will be booked for the full year, and expecting ~12-15% growth guidance to hold; management ambition of 20% growth stated but not committed.
FY27 EBITDA margin: management says Q1 is seasonally strongest, margins moderate in Q2-Q3 and recover in Q4; no firm FY27 margin expansion number given.
Medium term: Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years, driven by electronics and mechanisation mix.
FY28 revenue: Kanad Mukherjee said FY28 will 'definitely cross INR600 crore', with range INR630-640 crore and a target of above INR650 crore by FY28.
CCTV/projects: targeted ~INR30 crore revenue this year (vs INR13-14 crore last year) and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore vs ~INR2.5 crore last year.
Debt: management says no increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat over FY27-FY28.
Free cash flow: average INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by moving systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to ~INR30 crore.
capex_capacity: DDU-GKY Odisha skill project awarded for INR7.93 crore; management expects ~INR4 crore billing this year; about six-month infrastructure gestation period and two-year contract tenor.

HDFC Bank command-and-control centre (CCTV-driven, subscription model, covering 100-150 branches): management expects INR1.5-2 crore investment (about INR1 crore for control room) and INR2-3 crore revenue; final stage negotiations.
Mumbai traffic and police projects: INR15-18 crore expected from one or two tenders; an INR2.18 crore Mumbai traffic tender already received.
NKDA AMC contract worth about INR6 crore expected, pending final tendering; SAIL Burnpur engagement targeted at INR4-5 crore this year.
Acquisitions: management says acquisitions are possible in the future for technology capabilities, but not immediate; no near-term plans for manpower-based acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Q1 order wins: 5 work orders from Reliance Projects and Property Management Services worth INR30.77 crore; 7 Reliance Group FM contracts worth INR14.94 crore (combined INR45.71 crore); 2 Nesco orders worth INR1.94 crore; West Bengal Public Department housekeeping order INR36.71 lakh.
Government GeM tenders now at around 3.85% (L1 pricing); management says it will be more selective in manpower GeM bids and focus on CCTV and DDU-GKY projects.
Customer mix: Reliance top client at INR46-47 crore annually; HDFC Bank ~INR18 crore; Anjali Jewellers ~INR12 crore; airports ~INR30 crore annually; Torrent Power ~INR6-7 crore.
Renewal rates ~96-97%; average client retention 4.5-5 years per management.
Geographic mix: West Bengal ~72-73% of revenue; growth push in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Bihar and Odisha.
Receivable cycle: bills raised after wages; client payment typically in about three months.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone revenue (June 2026 quarter, as read out)
financial_highlights.value: INR110.53 crore: security INR54.98 crore, housekeeping INR41.88 crore, IFM INR10.28 crore, payroll INR3.40 crore
INR2.11 crore; PAT loss about INR1.27 lakh
Standalone ~INR69 crore debt vs ~INR60 crore cash (June); consolidated debt ~INR82 crore

qa_highlights.question: Given 12-15% FY27 growth guidance, Q1 growth of ~16% and ~8% margin, is there scope to raise FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 revenues booked from Nov-Dec onwards will be booked for the full year in FY27, and it is confident of crossing INR500 crore this year. Q1 EBITDA is seasonally better, moderating in Q2-Q3 and recovering in Q4, so no margin expansion percentage was committed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 FY27 revenue split by segment and how has the mix changed?
qa_highlights.answer: June 2026 quarter: security INR54.98 crore, housekeeping INR41.88 crore, IFM INR10.28 crore, payroll INR3.40 crore (total INR110.53 crore); CCTV INR2.11 crore; small security and housekeeping INR1.29 crore; vocational training nil. Manpower EBITDA about 9.95%; CCTV PAT loss about INR1.27 lakh; vocational training net loss about INR57 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and free cash flow target for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat. Average FCF was INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by growing systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to about INR30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth an aspiration, and how will margins move from ~7% to 8-9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hope is to grow 20% without compromising the balance sheet, but no commitment. On margins, Kanad Mukherjee said expansion depends on project businesses catching up with manpower business; Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years from electronics and mechanisation mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt, and why not a buyback given the share price fall since the IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone debt about INR69 crore vs cash about INR60 crore as of June; consolidated debt about INR82 crore. On the buyback proposal (13 lakh shares, about INR6 crore), Debajit Choudhury said the IPO capital is meant for growth, citing skill development capex, and did not commit to a buyback.

qa_highlights.question: Why was CCTV loss-making in Q1 and what is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Project businesses incur Q1 losses due to execution spend before completion certificates and billing; FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore. Management expects stabilisation by September quarter and targets about INR30 crore CCTV/projects revenue and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore this year. FY28: revenue to cross INR600 crore, range INR630-640 crore, target above INR650 crore.

risks_watch: Thin margin expansion visibility: management declined to give a firm FY27 margin number and expects Q2-Q3 moderation; medium-term 1-2% EBITDA uplift is the only figure given.
CCTV/projects execution: Q1 loss and reliance on lumpy tenders (Mumbai traffic INR15-18 crore, HDFC Bank command centre, NKDA AMC ~INR6 crore, SAIL INR4-5 crore) that are not yet awarded.
Pricing pressure in government manpower work: GeM L1 bids at about 3.85%, with management saying it will be more selective.
Working capital and receivables: about 3-month (90-day) client payment cycle; debt flat at about INR69 crore standalone and cash of INR60 crore as of June, with rising loans and advances.

Client concentration and renewal: Reliance at INR46-47 crore annually is the top client, and the DTET contract is under renewal with a loss already provided for; monitor renewal outcome and West Bengal concentration (72-73%).
Capital allocation and shareholder value: share price about INR46 vs IPO price INR111, buyback rejected in favour of growth capex; IPO funds unutilised INR36.85 crore as of June 2026.
key_quotes: So what we are seeing is that, last year we would have -- whatever revenues we had booked from November-December onwards that will get booked for the entire year during this financial year.
So whether there is going to be an expansion at the EBITDA margin at a percentage level is hard to say.
There will be no increase in debt. Debt levels will stay the same. There will be no increase in debt.
So I would expect at least an increase of about 1% to 2% in the EBITDA area over the next 2 years or so.
544495|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on order inflows, growth and FY28 revenue targets, but cautious and evasive on margin expansion, buybacks and the share price decline, which management largely deflected toward growth investment. Several answers were qualified with "hard to say" or "let's see", and the CCTV loss was framed as seasonal timing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions (plants, lines, branches) discussed; growth is order-led in manpower and project services, with only a minor HDFC command-centre control room (about INR1 crore) planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 consolidated income up 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore and Q1 work orders of INR45.71 crore support 12-15% FY27 growth guidance, with FY28 target of INR630-640 crore, a new figure implying ~25% growth on INR500 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is light (HDFC control room about INR1-2 crore, DDU-GKY infrastructure); management has rejected buyback in favour of growth capex from INR36.85 crore unutilised IPO funds, but no major capex plan was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident of crossing INR500 crore and reiterated FY28 INR630-640 crore, and says a 20% growth ambition is not committed; Q1 revenue grew 15.68% against 12-15% guidance, but no explicit raise was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects margin moderation in Q2-Q3, CCTV Q1 loss (PAT loss about INR1.27 lakh) with stabilisation only by September quarter, and GeM L1 pricing at about 3.85% pressures manpower bids.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Systems revenue to rise from INR13-14 crore to about INR30 crore this year via CCTV and command-centre subscription models (HDFC 100-150 branches, INR2-3 crore revenue), though no named product launch was given.

rows.why: Client payment typically takes about 3 months (working capital ~90 days) and standalone debt of INR69 crore vs cash INR60 crore leaves little buffer while management keeps debt flat.

rows.why: Q1 order wins of INR45.71 crore (Reliance and Nesco) are booked, but the INR15-18 crore Mumbai traffic and INR6 crore NKDA AMC tenders are not yet awarded and drive the CCTV ~INR30 crore target.

rows.label: FCF lift to INR13-14 crore
rows.why: Average FCF was INR8-9 crore over 3-4 years; target is to lift it to INR13-14 crore by growing systems revenue to about INR30 crore, but management also says debt stays flat.

tone.note: Management was confident on order inflows, the INR500 crore FY27 and INR630-650 crore FY28 revenue targets, but cautious and evasive on margin expansion, buyback and the share price fall, deflecting to growth capex; analysts pressed on net debt, buyback and margin path.

544496|2026-03.headline: Vikran FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,249 crore (vs INR916 crore) with EBITDA margin near 14%; FY27 guided at INR2,200 crore plus.
544496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR647 crore, up from INR355 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (14.2% margin) and PAT of INR56 crore (vs INR38 crore). For FY26, revenue rose to INR1,249 crore, EBITDA was about INR175 crore (around 14%) and PAT was INR92 crore (vs about INR78 crore). Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR355 crore in Q4 FY25
vs INR38 crore in Q4 FY25
vs INR916 crore in FY25; highest in company history
vs about INR78 crore in FY25
vs about INR2,000 crore earlier per CFO; management cited INR4,000-4,500 crore in a question
vs INR470 crore last year (per analyst)

financial_highlights.value: upgraded to IND A, stable outlook

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Management sees FY27 power T&D at about 30% of revenue, focused on selective 765 kV GIS/AIS projects for clients such as Power Grid and NTPC. Scope includes substations, lines, underground cabling and smart metering.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Solar is now the main growth pillar, with management expecting about 60% of FY27 revenue. Marquee wins include 100 MW AC (Ellume Energy), 400 MW AC / 580 MWp DC (NTPC Renewable) and 600 MW (NOPL Solar); 20 MW of NOPL is commissioned, with more due by end-May.

segments.name: Water infrastructure
segments.commentary: Water is about 10% of FY27 revenue from the existing order book, roughly INR600 crore; no new water bids for about 18 months. Jal Jeevan Mission receivables are about INR400 crore, and INR17-18 crore was received in FY27 to date.

segments.name: NOPL Solar (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Acquired 100% at end-April 2026; project cost INR4,200 crore with sanctioned lender funding. Management cites revenue over INR500 crore over 25 years, 85-88% EBITDA margin, and about INR1 crore per month from the first 20 MW.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue from operations guided at INR2,200 crore plus (CFO also cited INR2,200-2,500 crore), with or without NOPL, per management.
EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% for FY27, which management said it was confident of maintaining.
Possible additional INR1,000-1,400 crore solar EPC order from the Onix balance EPC scope, not yet in the INR5,700 crore order book; may be booked at arm's length price.
FY27 growth expected to be higher than FY26; FY28 revenue about INR3,000 crore plus; management declined to give FY29 figures.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive from FY28; management said no further equity dilution is planned.
Data centre EPC target of about INR100 crore order book in FY27, initially 50-100 MW.
MNRE and MSEDCL have extended the NOPL project deadline to March 2027.
capex_capacity: NOPL 969 MW PM-KUSUM project: 148 MW in advanced execution; about 85% of land identified since takeover; about 150 locations; 20 MW commissioned, with 20 MW more due in days.
Project funding of INR4,200 crore is sanctioned by a major lender, and the existing financing line rolls over to the new owner subject to a promoter evaluation; backup financing is in place.
Solar EPC: 500 MW EPC project in execution; company's total under-construction portfolio stated as about 1.5 GW (1 GW developer, 500 MW EPC).
Operational footprint: 22 states, 190 locations, about 1,200 staff, with about 222 at the Thane head office.
Management is cautiously evaluating Middle East and Africa opportunities, and says it is not pursuing a developer or investment model for data centres.
demand_pricing: Government push and private demand for solar; management sees better cash flow and margins in solar.
Management said it is selectively bidding; no new water orders for about 18 months.
Management said the company has no BESS in its current scope but has bid for some BESS projects.
Supply chain is largely dependent on China, but management says procurement was front-loaded in FY26 and the West Asia conflict has had limited impact so far.
Management says CFO-level margin for FY23-25 was 15-17%, and that projects are being chosen for similar margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin recover from 13-14% to historical 18-22%, and what is the status of the Onix project and its financing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY23-25 EBITDA was 15-17%, with FY26 at about 14% due to JJM receivable provisions (reversed on collection). Management said the Onix SPV is now 100% owned; the lender is comfortable, and 4 projects are commissioned with 2 more due by end-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is execution in FY27 with and without NOPL, and what milestones have been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says INR2,200 crore plus is achievable with or without NOPL, and that a plan without NOPL 'does not make a lot of sense'. Milestones since the April takeover are limited to a few commissioned projects; land and evacuation issues are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much receivables exposure is there from water/JJM, and how much was provided in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR400 crore of water receivables are due from JJM. About INR20 crore of provision was taken in FY26, mostly in Q4; the CFO said there is no specific high-risk receivable.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash flow turn positive, and will there be equity dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there are no plans for further equity dilution and that operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28; the order book has grown from about INR2,000 crore to over INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix for FY27?

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: is the Cheaper, Faster, Better flywheel now visible enough to call a bold trajectory shift in Services NTV growth, and can growth be guided higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: why should InstaHelp get capital and attention, and how will capital be allocated over two years between Services, new segments and international?
qa_highlights.answer: InstaHelp is strategically relevant because its high frequency keeps users on the app weekly. Services is to be profitable and cash generating; UAE and Singapore are profitable wholly owned subsidiaries; the Saudi JV is nearing profitability. InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: why not export the UAE and Saudi model to new international markets, given Core Services is generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bandwidth as the main constraint. It said playbooks need local customisation plus some luck, and that earlier Australia and US launches did not succeed. It will stay focused on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, with no plans for new international markets for now.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: where does Services margin go from 6.9% of NTV versus the 9-10% target, and would the company cap margin around 10% or reinvest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: is the InstaHelp TAM structurally lower, and would the company operate at a narrow loss if competition leaves room for only two players?
qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: what AOV is needed for InstaHelp to break even, and is there scope for growth above 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable professional payout is INR 130-160 per hour, with INR 150 as the rule of thumb. Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: Kotak: is Beauty acceleration sustainable, and are the 30-40 annual transactions per user assumption and consolidation prospects realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Beauty has seen a resurgence after retraining and retooling partners, and that the company had underinvested there a couple of years back. Two-wheeler access for Beauty professionals is now a majority. It expects 3 transactions per month, not 30-40, for the 10-12 lakh household case. It expects private players to keep burning cash and believes it will be the eventual winner in the category.

qa_highlights.question: Bellwether: what is driving the 5 lakh quarter-on-quarter user addition, what marketing spend is involved, and what training and capacity constraints exist in InstaHelp and Core Services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the user growth is largely from MAU, DAU and MTU growth and better conversion, and that marketing spend in Services was about INR 25 crore versus INR 24 crore a year ago. For Core, it said capacity is comfortable but is being scaled up, with all hands on deck, to match trainer and infrastructure growth. It said InstaHelp supply is also being expanded.

qa_highlights.question: Emkay: is the shift to premium products a sign of a premium customer base, and will the company expand beyond water purifiers and smart locks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its products, such as the M3 water purifier with a 3-year no-service, no-filter-change design, are aimed at lowering lifecycle cost. It said it is not building a durables company and will keep its focus on a small number of categories, mainly water purifiers and smart locks, with the aim of serving the top households in India.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses: the loss was INR (132) crore; management expects 2+ years of investment and an adjusted breakeven target within about 18 months. Track loss per order, which improved from INR (447) in Q4 to INR (346) in Q1.
AOV and payout economics: InstaHelp needs about INR 300 AOV to break even, with pay of INR 130-160 per hour; competitor pricing of INR 80-120 per hour is a pressure point.
Competition and TAM: management said 3 major players have limited coverage to 3.5-4 million households; the TAM base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore against a bull case of INR 10,000-12,000 crore.
Growth sustainability: Services NTV growth of 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base, and management declined to give forward growth guidance.
Services margin: current 6.9% of NTV against a 9-10% long-term target; the timing of expansion remains unspecified.
Capacity and trainer scaling for Core Services as user additions accelerate.

rows.why: Total orders rose 79% YoY to 13.2 million, 1.2 million new customers were added, InstaHelp orders grew 43% QoQ to 3.82 million, and Services NTV growth accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29%, though management gave no forward growth number.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: AI-driven efficiency in Services

544515|2026-09.headline: Urban Company's consolidated NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore in Q2 FY27, with adjusted EBITDA (ex-Native/International investment) at ₹30 crore, up 213% YoY.
544515|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated NTV up 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and revenue from operations up 41.4% to ₹537.3 crore, with adjusted loss of ₹144 crore after a ₹174 crore investment in Native. Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments, and management reiterated breakeven for the consolidated business by Q3 FY28 and a ₹1,000 crore EBITDA-type goal for FY31. Management announced a fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore, framed as flexibility rather than a need to fund losses. Q&A focused on the rationale for the raise, Native's AC launch, professional supply, and pricing/contribution economics.

financial_highlights.change: +213% YoY; ₹119 crore for trailing four quarters, +175%
vs NTV growth of 26%, per management
up 110 bps (from prior level per call)

segments.name: Core Services (India)
segments.commentary: Management said Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments and contribution margin rose to 3.5%; NTV growth was attributed to new-customer acquisition, repeat cohorts and densification, with instant service now used in top 7–8 cities.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
segments.commentary: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY per management, with UAE described as a key market; adjusted EBITDA margin was 2% of NTV, improved by 190 bps. Management said war-related concerns are behind it and Q2+Q3 combined growth is expected at 50–55%.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers / AC services)
segments.commentary: Native's loss narrowed by ₹220 crore (per call) with loss per order down 19% QoQ to ₹279; management says Native is being built deliberately with a ₹174 crore investment in Q2 and is in a learning phase for its first AC device.

segments.name: Insta Help (professional/household help)
segments.commentary: Management said Insta Help is in a tougher base with Q2 revenue growth at 26.3% and the festive season falling in Q3; penetration in top 8 cities for largest categories is below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated breakeven target reiterated for Q3 FY28; management said it is confident, more than ever, of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal.
Management expects Q2 plus Q3 combined international growth in the range of 50% to 55%.
Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is for flexibility, mainly for organic build-out of existing businesses and selective M&A; management said nothing imminent.
Native AC device launch: management expects one to two quarters of learning, limited largely to the app, and no material change to Native's trajectory.
Contribution margin target of 9–10% noted as the key lever; management said it is working towards it.
capex_capacity: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million; 45% of new orders are reportedly from the Core Services' top categories, per management.
Management is onboarding professionals aggressively in the 3–4 months before the festive season to improve the liquidity coefficient.
Native's offline distribution is in a learning phase; M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra launched in modern retail with pull from offline ecosystem.
Gold premium service rollout: management said results are promising and it intends to scale it out across categories.
demand_pricing: Core Services average spend growth slowed to around 3% (vs historical 6–7%); management attributed this to mix change and season timing, and pass-through of densification benefits in pockets.
Instant service delivered in 30–60 minutes is offered in UAE and Singapore; management said no premium is currently charged.
Professional (partner) supply grew 16% YoY versus NTV growth of 26%; management declined to give forward partner-growth projections.
Hourly pricing roughly ₹200 and net order value roughly ₹300 for an average order of 1.5 hours; partner payout of ₹150 per utilised hour.
Management described the household-help TAM as range-bound with no single winner, and the AC TAM as roughly 10x water purifier TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Core Services' accelerating new-user acquisition and is it sustainable, with average spend growth slowing to 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a stronger product with instant service in top 7–8 cities, AI-led training/QC improving word of mouth, densification, faster growth in Tier-2 markets and higher marketing. Average spend slowed due to mix, seasonality and some densification benefit passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of proceeds from the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and the M&A framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly for flexibility and organic build-out; M&A would be for consolidating existing categories or entering new categories, not new countries, with buy-vs-build tilting to buy if accretive. Nothing imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise capital now given cash on balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is for flexibility, to be aggressive, pursue acquisitions and absorb downside in a high-competition scenario; not primarily to fund losses. Targets remain unchanged, and they would have changed short/medium-term targets if funding were insufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Native AC launch and its allocation impact profitability timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.

More guarded on specifics: declined to give partner-growth projections, did not quantify average-spend slowdown beyond mix and seasonality, and said the AC launch would be calibrated and slow.

544516|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 66% to Rs.319.6 Crores with PAT margin of 12.2%; FY27 guidance is Rs.500 Crores revenue at 12-13% PAT margin.
544516|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs.319.6 Crores (up 66% YoY), with H2 contributing Rs.229.1 Crores (up 114% YoY), and EBITDA of Rs.64.2 Crores at a 20.1% margin (EBITDA margin down from about 25% per analyst question). PAT was Rs.39.1 Crores (up 52%) at a 12.2% margin. Management said the Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly because it declined to pursue low-margin re-tenders amid aluminium and stainless steel inflation. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs.500 Crores at 12-13% PAT margin, backed by an unexecuted order book of about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure varied in the call) and a Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: +66% YoY vs Rs.192.4 Crores in FY25
+114% YoY vs Rs.107.3 Crores in H2 FY25
receivable days down 24 days; inventory days down 48 days

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver; management says about 70% of the pipeline is railway, roughly Rs.900 Crores of the Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline, covering Atmanirbhar Bharat, Spark and Kavach coaches, Vande Bharat sleeper and Amrit Bharat turnkey contracts. Refurbishment is cited as a separate opportunity of about Rs.26,000 Crores sanctioned, with hoped-for orders of at least Rs.100 Crores this year.

segments.name: Metro
segments.commentary: About Rs.70 Crores of metro orders held, with another Rs.120 Crores expected within the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline; Kolkata Metro turnkey contracts are named as a focus.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Rs.29 Crores of current order book to execute this year, plus Rs.60-70 Crores expected from HAL tenders (mainly simulators, not AMCA airframe production). Proposed JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions to be incorporated before 15 June 2026; Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores, focused on autonomous drones and electronic warfare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of approximately Rs.500 Crores with PAT margin of 12-13%; management said PAT would not fall below 12%.
Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly; management also said it could be reached in FY28 or earlier if conditions allow.
Management said about 70-75% of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.
R&D spend to rise to about 8-9% of sales this year from about 4% earlier; management later said R&D spend would be capitalised on the balance sheet.
Capex of Rs.30-40 Crores planned for FY27-28, including about Rs.30-35 Crores for a 14-acre facility with 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft of initial shed space, expanding to 3-4 lakh sq ft.
Debt funding of about Rs.120 Crores at 8.25% from two banks: Rs.60 Crores sanctioned, the other Rs.60 Crores expected by end June 2026. No equity raise planned this year.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation is about 90% of existing facility; two-shift operations in use since around December 2025.
New 14-acre facility planned: initial 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft, later extending to 3-4 lakh sq ft; land already acquired and term loan discussions with bankers under way.

Machinery purchases, mostly from China, delayed because Chinese OEMs require an end-user certificate from the Government of India; management expected clarity in June 2026 and may switch to different machinery for lightweight rail interiors.
Plans to consolidate seven units into about two, reducing rent of roughly Rs.20-25 lakh per month.
Channel partner model in place to execute zonal railway contracts without building facilities in each region.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure cited differently in different answers): Rs.415-420 Crores government and Rs.50-55 Crores non-government.
Bid pipeline about Rs.1,200 Crores with historical bid-win ratio of about 20-25%.

Raw material inflation: aluminium up more than 80% and stainless steel up 60-65% YoY; price variation clauses cover only about 50-60% of the increase, and accessories (30-35% of assembly cost) are not covered.
Competitors named: Kineco, Hindustan Fiberglass Works, DTL Ancillaries, Vibgyor, Universal Engineers; seating competitors Tata (with Fainsa), a Korean firm and firms from Mumbai and Bengaluru.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about Rs.100-110 Crores of receivables collected by June end; receivable and working capital cycles targeted at 60-70 days from 90-95 days within 3-4 months. Debt of Rs.120 Crores is being raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-75% is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Margin pressure and its causes in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium and stainless steel inflation hit margins. Management said price variation covers only about 50-60% of losses, and it used advances, LCs and BGs to block vendor prices, limiting losses to 20-25% of the uncovered amount.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of added debt interest and R&D on the 12-13% PAT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would stay at or above 12%, citing higher-margin bids and that R&D spend would be deployed only when expected returns are met.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 revenue reach Rs.1,000 Crores and PAT Rs.150 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000 Crores could be reached even this year if all goes well and that FY28 could exceed Rs.1,000 Crores, without firm numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.500 Crores target hold given 90% utilisation and machinery delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery delays would not affect FY27 turnover; two-shift operation and channel partners could add Rs.400-450 Crores from the Rs.320 Crores base.

544516|2026-09.headline: Airfloa H1 FY26 net profit rose 24% YoY to INR12.09 crore on INR90.98 crore total income; order book crossed INR455 crore.
544516|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY26 total income of INR90.98 crore (up nearly 7% YoY), EBITDA of INR22.46 crore and net profit of INR12.09 crore (up 24% YoY), its first results call after the BSE SME listing in September 2025. Active order book was stated at over INR455 crore after a recent INR1,013 crore order win in a single week from ICF and MCF. Management guided to FY26 turnover of over INR300 crore and FY27 of at least INR550 crore, with defence (drones, anti-drone, laser systems via a JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions) as a stated growth driver. Capacity is being expanded through a 14-acre plant purchase, with a term loan under discussion.

544523|2026-03.headline: FY26 gross sales rose 19.5% to INR 2,913.9 crore and normalised PAT grew about 20% to INR 102.3 crore; FY27 guided to 18-20% revenue and 20-22% PAT growth.

544523|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 gross sales rose 5.7% to INR 641.2 crore while PAT jumped 51.7% to INR 15.7 crore on margin recovery.
544523|2026-06.overview: Gross sales were INR 641.2 crore (up 5.7% YoY) and gross margin widened to 8.1% of gross sales from 6.8%, lifting gross margin INR 52 crore (up 26.5%). Operating EBITDA was INR 20.2 crore (up 27.7%) and PAT INR 15.7 crore (up 51.7%), helped by lower finance costs. Cybersecurity grew 8% and DCI grew about 180%, while ILM fell about 60% as customer budgets shifted toward GPU and data-centre spend. Management reiterated 20% growth in gross sales and PAT for FY27 and said H2 is seasonally stronger. The CEO is stepping down, with the Chairman/MD and Executive Director jointly overseeing the role.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ILM fall about 60% YoY and is cybersecurity slowing versus peers growing 25-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ILM's fall to budgets reallocated to GPU and data-centre spend and expects ILM to return from Q3. It said cybersecurity is growing and is expected to be 45-50% of sales annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 gross sales soft and why has gross profit growth lagged guidance for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY26 base had a large GSTN deal of about INR 150 crore billed in Q2 and that large deals cluster in H2. It said the Q1 FY26 margin was depressed by rupee depreciation and low-margin deals, so a 10% gross profit growth in FY26 is not the steady-state rate.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 46% annuity share mean net new sales are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annuity was 43.1% in Q1 FY26 and that the roughly 3-point rise came from upsell and price increases at existing customers, not a hit to net new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company benefit from data-centre build-outs such as Reliance-Meta?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishna Raj Sharma said public data centres mostly contract directly with OEMs, so the larger opportunity is private/captive data centres. Sunil Pillai said the TAM will be sized once capacity is online.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CEO be replaced and is inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CEO is leaving for personal reasons and that the Chairman/MD and Executive Director will jointly oversee the role, with new CBO, CRO and CTO appointed. Inorganic growth is being explored, with no material progress announced.

qa_highlights.question: Are OEM acquisitions by Palo Alto, Cisco or IBM a risk to accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Pillai said consolidation has been ongoing for two to three years and that the company has not seen revenue loss from it, and may gain access to acquired products.

544523|2026-09.headline: iValue Q2 FY27 gross sales fell 17.6% YoY to INR 731.6 crores on a high base; management reiterates ~20% FY27 top-line and PAT growth guidance.
544523|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 gross sales rose 14% QoQ to INR 731.6 crores but fell 17.6% YoY against a base that included a roughly INR 150 crore large deal in Q2 FY26. H1 gross sales were INR 1,372.8 crores, down 8.1%, while H1 PAT fell 2.4% to INR 39.1 crores. Q2 results were flattered by a one-time high-margin deal and a INR 3.7 crore land-sale gain, and hit by a INR 4.4 crore receivable write-off from a single Indian partner. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% growth in top line and PAT, citing a tracked pipeline of INR 6,900 crores (up from INR 6,149 crores QoQ) and October billings that already exceed the full Q3 FY26 figure.

segments.name: Cybersecurity (largest, ~48% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 sales down 8.7% YoY. Management cites large-deal timing and customer budget deferrals; DPDP-related deals are being signed.

segments.name: Data center infrastructure (~19% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 growth of 39.7% YoY; budgets reportedly shifting from ILM toward DCI.

segments.name: Information lifecycle management (ILM, ~14% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 sales down 48.1% YoY, driven by deferral of deals from one large OEM into Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: ALM, cloud and others (~19% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 growth of 27.2% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 guidance reiterated as directional: ~20% top-line growth and ~20% PAT growth over FY26; management says it will narrow guidance at the Q3 call.
Management assumes an H1:H2 split of 40:60, implying full-year gross sales of about INR 3,430 crores and H2 of about INR 2,000 crores (~50% growth over H1).
Gross margin for FY27 expected around the current ~9% level or slightly above; medium-term net gross margin band of 9% to 9.5%, with overall margin between 9% and 10%.
Around 70% of incremental gross margin expected to flow to EBITDA, supporting an EBITDA margin expansion of about 20 to 25 bps in the medium term.
Annuity share of gross sales expected to end FY27 near 50% (plus or minus 1%), with absolute annuity sales rising in H2.
Capital allocation decision (acquisition, dividend, buyback or bonus) to follow if no acquisition target is found in FY27, likely at Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex plans were discussed on the call.

International push: ASEAN engagement (Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam) and CLM region through OEM and ecosystem partners; headcount added in ASEAN, worth about INR 1 to 1.5 crores of the H1 manpower increase.
Cloud: partnered with one hyperscaler and running a dedicated motion for hybrid workload migration, with results expected in coming quarters.
Manpower cost H1 FY27 INR 40.9 crores vs INR 35.5 crores in H1 FY26 (+15%), driven by new hires, ASEAN investment and 8-10% appraisals from 1 July.
demand_pricing: Large deals are defined as above INR 100 crores; the company typically wins 2 to 3 a year and is working on 5 to 6 large deals currently, with some at L1 stage and none lost.
Pipeline INR 6,900 crores vs INR 6,149 crores last quarter (~12% QoQ). Billings for October plus bookings convertible in the quarter already exceed full Q3 FY26 billings.

Customers are delaying awards by 2 to 3 months and negotiating heavily with SIs after L1 selection, citing hardware and component price inflation. Some customers are opting for renewals over tech refresh, boosting annuity renewals.
Margin pressure from OEM price negotiations is present but has been limited so far, per management.
OEM consolidation has occurred, but no revenue or margin hit so far; the company has signed other OEMs in the same space and has a funnel running.
A customer default by an Indian partner led to a INR 4.4 crore write-off after a settlement; the Q2 one-time gain of INR 3.7 crores came from sale of vacant land (non-operating income).

qa_highlights.question: Early indicators for Q3, and what would the Q3 colour look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited large deals moving closer to conversion and October billings plus next two months' convertible bookings already exceeding full Q3 FY26 billings, with about 45 days left in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 20% guidance need INR 600-700 crores per quarter, and is it large-deal led or higher conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large deals are binary, so a 6-month conversion rate can look above 35%; annuity share should fall to about 50% by year-end as large and net new deals land in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H2 guidance imply ~50% growth, and is it confident?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; applying the 40:60 H1:H2 ratio to H1 sales of INR 1,372 crores gives FY27 of about INR 3,430 crores and H2 of about INR 2,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why was non-annuity sales only about INR 295 crores in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are negotiating after award and extending renewals to preserve budget for other spend, which shifted mix toward annuity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 28% in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 manpower cost rose 15% to INR 40.9 crores, from new hires for growth, ASEAN investment (INR 1 to 1.5 crores) and 8-10% appraisals.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of forex on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Payables are hedged, but a mark-to-market impact of about INR 1 crore hit P&L in the period as of 30 September.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cybersecurity incidents lift demand, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees an uptick but expects the benefit mainly in FY28, as customers are unlikely to change budgets mid-year; deferred tech refreshes are also expected to come through.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the DPDP opportunity and will local OEMs be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marquee DPDP deals are already signed, with more opportunities in Q3 and Q4, and it expects Indian OEMs to be a large part of the opportunity.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on a small number of large Q3 and Q4 deals; any slippage from 31 March to 1 April-type timing would shift the quarter.

ILM decline of 48.1% in H1 depends on the large OEM's deals moving into Q3 and Q4.
Further OEM consolidation could hit revenue; management has not seen an impact yet.
Other expenses rose about 35% YoY including the write-off; management says ~15-18% excluding it. Watch for further partner credit issues.
Watch Q3 FY27 results for conversion of the INR 6,900 crore pipeline, narrowing of guidance, and annuity share trend.

Installations of 61,000+ systems in FY26 (up 34%) fell short of the 70,000-75,000 guidance, which management attributed to rainfall in Maharashtra and raw material delays in late March. Installations more than doubled to 24,118 systems, and 109 MW of renewable capacity was commissioned, taking the cumulative base to over 164,500 systems and 726 MW. 544526|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 111% to INR 45,484 million, but Q4 EBITDA margin compressed sharply on input-cost inflation and rupee depreciation.
544526|2026-03.overview: Saatvik reported record FY26 revenue of INR 45,484 million (up about 111% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5,811 million (12.78% margin) and PAT of INR 3,571 million (7.85% margin). Q4 revenue hit a record INR 16,077 million, but EBITDA fell to INR 1,166 million and PAT to INR 604 million, as silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked input costs rose and the rupee weakened after the war that began 20 February 2026. Management said fixed-price contracts could not pass on these increases immediately. Cell capacity expansion is the main near-term story: 2.4 GW cell line is targeted to start production in H2 FY27, and the cell plan is now 6 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA decline, and what margins do new orders carry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked costs, rupee depreciation, and fixed-price contracts signed before the war that could not be repriced immediately. Some new orders can pass costs through and others must absorb them, depending on the customer.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 2.4 GW and 6 GW cell lines start and stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Module equipment move-in starts June 2026 and cell equipment move-in July 2026, with production starting in H2 FY27. Phase II (3.6 GW) civil work starts August 2026; full 6 GW by June-July 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27-FY28 capex and debt plans?

qa_highlights.question: Why has cash conversion been low, and why did creditor days fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Large PSU orders carry 90-120 day recovery cycles, with Q4 dispatches recovering in April-May. Creditor days normalised as the company paid suppliers faster to secure better pricing during the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will cells be sold externally, and what are the EPC and order-execution details?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6 GW cell capacity is currently for captive use, but management will decide on external sales based on margins. Execution timeline is about 18 months, EPC contribution is about 3-4% and stays in that range in FY27.

544526|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn (from INR 9,157 mn YoY) on 334 MW sales; EBITDA margin rose to 8.33% while confirmed order book stands at ~6.35 GW.
544526|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: sales of 334 MW were down from 579 MW a year earlier and 1,050 MW in Q4 FY26, as customers deferred procurement and management chose to execute only margin-accretive orders. Revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn and PAT to INR 54 mn. Management said the EBITDA margin of 8.33% was better than the 7.25% in Q4 FY26. The Odisha cell line (2.4 GW) is near ramp-up with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026, and management is pinning margin recovery on cell volumes in H2 FY27. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, but the call contained no numbers for Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
