rows.why: 2.4 GW cell line has tool move-in done with ~200 MW/month ramp planned and ~80% utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27; Phase 2 adds 3.6 GW cell by end-FY28, though slip risk exists with ALMM-2 inspection set for September 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 sales fell 42% YoY to 334 MW (vs 579 MW) and 68% QoQ from 1,050 MW; FY27 guide of 3.5-4 GW needs roughly 3.2-3.7 GW in Q2-Q4 (about 1.1-1.2 GW/quarter), versus a 334 MW Q1 base, and no Q2 number was given, while the 6.35 GW order book and cell ramp support recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Phase 2 site work by end-Q2 FY27; encapsulant equipment anno
rows.why: Phase 2 (3.6 GW cell, INR 1,600-1,700 crore) is already approved with site work starting by end-Q2 FY27, Phase 3 (6 GW ingot/wafer) planning has started, and the encapsulant capacity expansion from 2 GW to 5 GW is due to be announced next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was held unchanged despite Q1 sales of 334 MW and revenue of INR 5,110 mn, and management gave no Q2 numbers, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn vs INR 16,077 mn in Q4 FY26, FY27 guidance of ~INR 6,000 crore implies roughly INR 8,900 mn/quarter over Q2-Q4, and any cell ramp or ALMM-2 slip (to 1 January 2027) would push the 12% EBITDA margin case back.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DCR cell sales for own use have started with DCR cell margins quoted at 18-20%, and the non-module business (Melcon acquired mid-Q1) is targeted to rise from 4-5% to 7-8% of revenue in FY27 and 15% next year.

rows.label: 6.35 GW confirmed order book executing over 12-18 months
rows.why: Order book of about 6.35 GW (132% of 4.8 GW module capacity), valued at about INR 8,200 crore, with fresh orders of INR 138 crore (execution by Dec 2026) and about INR 400 crore (execution by Mar 2027) support near-term volumes.

rows.label: ALMM-2 inspection and postponed effective date
rows.why: ALMM-2 was postponed from 1 July 2026 to 1 January 2027 due to domestic cell shortages, and the inspection is planned for September 2026, which gates DCR cell demand and the cell-led margin thesis.

rows.label: Net debt peak of INR 2,200-2,400 crore
rows.why: Total debt is about INR 1,250 crore with debt-to-equity at 0.99x and about INR 1,000 crore of the roughly INR 3,500 crore capex programme spent, so net debt is set to rise before any deleveraging.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Odisha cell ramp and the integration story but cautious on near-term numbers: no Q2 figures, FY28 deferred to Q3 FY27, and the high-double-digit cell EBITDA uplift left unquantified; analysts pushed on the sharp YoY margin compression and volume decline.

544526|2026-09.headline: Saatvik Q2 FY27 revenue rose 77% QoQ to INR9,026 million, with EBITDA margin at 7.7% and order book at 6.68 GW.
544526|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR9,026 million, up 77% sequentially from INR5,110 million, but down from INR7,680 million a year earlier. EBITDA was INR696 million (7.7% margin) versus 8.3% in Q1, and PAT rose to INR202 million from INR54 million in Q1 but fell from INR847 million a year ago. Odisha module commercial production began on 2 November 2026 (1.3 GW of phase one), while the 2.4 GW cell line is in trial run and targeted for ramp-up by December 2026. Leverage rose sharply, with debt-to-equity at 1.37x versus 0.99x in June 2026 and 0.44x a year ago.

financial_highlights.change: +77% QoQ vs INR5,110 million; vs INR7,680 million in Q2 FY26
vs INR425 million, 8.3% in Q1 FY27; INR1,263 million in Q2 FY26
vs INR54 million in Q1 FY27; INR847 million in Q2 FY26
vs INR16,838 million in H1 FY26
vs 334 MW in Q1 FY27; 538 MW in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR13.49/Wp in Q2; INR13.89/Wp in H1

financial_highlights.change: vs 0.99x in June 2026 and 0.44x a year ago

financial_highlights.value: INR5,001 million capex; CWIP INR8,842 million
financial_highlights.change: CWIP up from INR3,841 million in March 2026

financial_highlights.value: Inventories INR9,074 million; receivables INR4,855 million; trade payables INR4,705 million
financial_highlights.change: Inventories up from INR7,016 million in March 2026; receivables down from INR6,988 million

segments.name: Modules (domestic and export)
segments.commentary: Q2 production was 658 MW (Q1: 408 MW) and sales 640 MW; H1 production 1,066 MW and sales 973 MW. Modules were about 96% of H1 revenue, and domestic customers were 96.7% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: Other businesses (EPC, solar pumps, transformers, inverters, encapsulants, batteries)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR408 million of revenue in Q2 and INR634 million in H1. Management says the share of non-module revenue rose to about 4% from 2.5-3% a year earlier, with a target of about 15% within two years.

segments.name: Revenue mix (per management, FY27 to date)
segments.commentary: C&I about 28%, utility about 52-55%, retail about 12%, exports about 3%, other about 4%.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to revenue of about INR6,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12%. This was stated for FY28, after the speaker first said FY27 and then corrected it.
Odisha module capacity to reach 4 GW by December 2026, taking total module capacity to 8.8 GW (Ambala 4.8 GW plus Odisha).
Cell line of 2.4 GW to see production ramp-up by December 2026 and 97-98% yield in the last quarter of FY27. Management expects EBITDA to rise in the last four months of FY27 as cell output starts.
Benefit from cell backward integration expected to start partially in Q3 and to show more clearly in Q4 FY27, with margins said to be in line with cell-integrated peers.
Next year (FY28) module utilisation targeted in the 80s; cell utilisation targeted above 90%.
Phase two (27 acres) adds 3.6 GW cells for a total of 6 GW, targeted for FY28. Phase three adds 6 GW ingot and wafer, targeted for FY29.
capex_capacity: Odisha phase one (57 acres): 1.3 GW module line commissioned with consent to operate received days before the call. Remaining 2.7 GW of modules targeted by December 2026, taking module capacity to 8.8 GW.
Cell capacity: 2.4 GW line in trial run and ramp-up. ALMM List-II inspection planned for November 2026 and expected by end-November. Ramp-up established by end-December.
Encapsulant capacity: 2 GW live, expanding by 3 GW to 5 GW by FY28.
Ingot and wafer: 6 GW planned for FY29, aligned with ALMM List-III from June 2028. Planning has started.
Module utilisation was 58.5% in Q2 and 47.4% in H1 (FY26 was about 85%). Effective capacity utilisation is expected to improve in H2 with Odisha coming on stream.
demand_pricing: Confirmed order book was 6.68 GW at 30 Sep 2026, about 110% of 6.1 GW installed module capacity. Order book was about 60% DCR and about 40% non-DCR.
Q2 order inflow was 970 MW and H1 inflow was 1.76 GW. Q2 execution was 640 MW and H1 execution was 970 MW.
Recent wins: Vikran Engineering INR476 crore (Aug), domestic module orders about INR190 crore (Aug) and INR297.5 crore (Sep), SECI INR1,041 crore (Sep), MSEDCL INR100 crore (Oct).
Current prices cited: TOPCon around INR20-21/Wp in utility; non-DCR around INR12-13/Wp. Management said these are current prices, not FY28 delivery prices.

Market context: India added about 20.8 GW of solar in H1 FY27 after a record 44.6 GW in FY26. Annual demand is expected to rise from about 50 GW in FY27 to 85 GW by FY30. Domestic cell capacity is about 37 GW against more than 200 GW of module capacity.
Management said about 70-80 GW of non-DCR orders remain in the system. Open access is estimated at 20-25 GW of opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations by segment (DCR, non-DCR, utility, retail, C&I), and how do they compare with peers' INR20-21/Wp quotes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TOPCon prices are around INR20-21/Wp and non-DCR around INR12.5-13/Wp, describing these as current prices rather than FY28 deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of China's technology-transfer export controls on cell and wafer capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the measures are being watched (expected around 15 November). Phase two cell groundbreaking is done, technology tie-ups are in place, and the company does not expect projects to be delayed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SuryaConnect solar kit's business model and competitive edge?
qa_highlights.answer: The kit is sold through distributors and online and installed by local IEC-registered players. The company has about 85-90 distributors/resellers and is adding more, targeting district and village coverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for EPC, pumps and BESS, and what revenue share is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: The aim is to raise the company's share of project cost from about 50-60% (modules) toward 70-80% by adding inverters and transformers. Non-module revenue is about 4% now, with a target of about 15% within two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY28 revenue and EBITDA guidance, and does it refer to FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR6,000 crore revenue and about 12% EBITDA margin. It was first described as FY27, then clarified as FY28. Management also said H2 FY27 EBITDA should rise as cell output starts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commissioning status and utilisation timeline for Odisha?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1.3 GW module line got consent to operate a few days earlier, with ALMM inspection in progress and revenue expected within 2-3 weeks. Cell ALMM inspection is expected by end-November, with the remaining modules in December. Management expects 97-98% cell yield in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the wafers for Odisha cells sourced, and how will import dependence be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term wafer contracts are in place with tier-one Chinese suppliers, and small-volume cell production has started. A 6 GW ingot and wafer plant is planned in Odisha to meet ALMM List-III from June 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What margin uplift is expected from cell backward integration, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits begin partially in Q3 FY27 and show clearly in Q4. Margins are expected to be in line with cell-integrated peers, and no specific number was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DCR margin, and what utilisation is expected in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR margins should be in line with peers, without giving a number. Module utilisation was about 58% in FY27 to date and is targeted in the 80s in FY28; cell utilisation is targeted above 90%.

risks_watch: Leverage: debt-to-equity rose to 1.37x from 0.99x in June 2026. Management said it is conscious of leverage during the build phase.
Execution: Odisha module ramp to 4 GW by December, cell ALMM-II inspection and yield ramp to 97-98%. Any slippage would delay the margin uplift.
Policy: ALMM List-II (cells) effective 1 June 2026, with a timeline reportedly reversed in July, and a Jan 2027 start mentioned. ALMM List-III from June 2028 requires own ingot and wafer capacity.
Technology-transfer restrictions from China (announcement around 15 November) could affect cell and wafer equipment timing. Management views the impact as limited.
Pricing: non-DCR pricing near INR12.5-13/Wp and raw material and module price corrections, which management did not quantify as to how they will be managed.
Working capital: inventories rose to INR9,074 million and CWIP to INR8,842 million. Watch cash conversion as Odisha assets go live.
key_quotes: I am pleased to share that commercial production at our 1.3 gigawatt module manufacturing facility in Gopalpur commenced successfully on 2nd November, 2026, and we expect the full 4 gigawatt capacity to be in place by December 2026.
I do not think it will be fair to give those numbers. This year is particularly a realignment year because ALMM List-I and ALMM List-II transition is happening.
We are conscious that leverage has risen during the build phase.
In terms of our margins, we cannot give a number, but it will be in line with our peers who are already in cell manufacturing.
544526|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the Odisha build-out, order book and policy direction, but cautious on leverage, FY28 utilisation and cell-linked margins. Management declined to give numbers on FY28 module and cell utilisation and on margin uplift, calling them forward-looking, and admitted FY27 is a "realignment year" with the ALMM transition reversed in July.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects cell backward integration to start partially in Q3 and show clearly in Q4 FY27, with EBITDA rising in the last four months, though Q2 EBITDA margin was 7.7% vs 8.3% in Q1 and no uplift number was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Odisha 1.3 GW module line already commissioned (commercial production from 2 Nov 2026), remaining 2.7 GW targeted by Dec 2026 taking module capacity to 8.8 GW, and 2.4 GW cell line in trial run with ramp-up by Dec 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 execution was 640 MW and H1 1.76 GW inflow against a 6.68 GW order book (about 110% of 6.1 GW installed capacity), but module utilisation was only 58.5% in Q2, so volume growth depends on Odisha ramp and conversion of orders.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Phase two cell (3.6 GW, total 6 GW) groundbreaking is done and phase three 6 GW ingot/wafer is planned for FY29 with planning started, though utilisation is low (58.5%), which tempers the need for new capex announcements.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The INR6,000 crore revenue and 12% EBITDA margin guidance is for FY28 and was already held, while H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 7.9% and H1 revenue fell to INR14,136 million from INR16,838 million.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Module utilisation was 47.4% in H1 vs about 85% in FY26, leverage rose to 1.37x D/E, and the ALMM policy timeline was reversed in July, so execution slippage on Odisha ramp or cell yield could cut the margin path.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cell output from the 2.4 GW line is targeted to start in Q3 and ramp with 97-98% yield by Q4 FY27, and non-module offerings (EPC, pumps, inverters, transformers, batteries) are being built toward a 15% revenue share within two years.

rows.label: Order book of 6.68 GW at 30 Sep 2026
rows.why: Confirmed order book of 6.68 GW is about 110% of 6.1 GW installed module capacity, with Q2 inflow 970 MW and recent wins including SECI INR1,041 crore and Vikran INR476 crore.

rows.label: Leverage rising during build phase
rows.why: Debt-to-equity rose to 1.37x from 0.99x in June 2026 and 0.44x a year ago, with CWIP at INR8,842 million, and management said it is conscious of leverage, so deleveraging is not signalled.

rows.label: Inventory build and cash conversion
rows.why: Inventories rose to INR9,074 million from INR7,016 million in March 2026 while receivables fell to INR4,855 million, so cash conversion as Odisha goes live is a watch item.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Odisha build-out, order book and policy direction but cautious on leverage, FY28 utilisation and cell-linked margins, declining to quantify them; analysts pushed on realisations versus peer quotes, the FY27 versus FY28 guidance mix-up, and cell margin uplift.

544527|2026-03.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 81.7% YoY to INR747.6 crore with EBITDA margin near 20%; FY26 term debt fully repaid.
544527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR747.6 crore (+81.7% YoY, +58.5% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR149.6 crore (19.99% margin vs 16.7% a year earlier) and PAT of INR102.2 crore (+128.9% YoY). Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR1,851.5 crore (+48.8%), EBITDA INR344.4 crore (18.6% margin, +300 bps) and PAT INR201.8 crore (+70.1%). All term loans were repaid by 31 March 2026, and the Vadod unit 4 received PGCIL approval for up to 400 kV on 2 April 2026. Management flagged a planned inventory drawdown ahead of April maintenance shutdowns and a mineral oil shortage in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.change: +117.9% YoY; margin vs 16.7% in Q4 FY25
up from INR910 crore; mainly non-fund based

segments.name: Vadod unit 4 (new)
segments.commentary: Produced 6,960 MVA in about seven months from July 2025 start, roughly 39% of 30,000 MVA nameplate; dispatched about 15 transformers per month in each of the last three months of FY26. Investment about INR200 crore; management cites Vadod revenue of about INR495 crore in first seven months.

segments.name: Atlanta Trafo unit 5 (Ankhi)
segments.commentary: Contributed 580 MVA in about three months during Q3 FY26; focused on 765 kV class prototype.

segments.name: Legacy units (Anand and Bengaluru, three units)
segments.commentary: Ran at very high utilisation through FY26. Total FY26 output across five units was 22,943 MVA.

segments.name: 220 kV and above mix
segments.commentary: 220 kV class constitutes nearly 52% of revenue; management says margins on 220 kV and below are expected to remain stable.

guidance_outlook: Vadod utilisation expected at about 65% in FY27 and 100% in FY28; mainstream 400 kV production from FY28 would take capacity to 30,000 MVA.
Management targets about 40% revenue CAGR for the next three years; margins guided to stay stable, within an 18-20% band.
Net working capital days expected to rise to around 80-90 in FY27 and FY28 as higher-kV mix grows.
400/765 kV products expected to carry about 200 bps higher margin, but R&D, technical tie-up and type-testing costs will offset this near term.
Exports targeted at 15% of total revenue within three years; first export breakthrough expected in FY27, with execution in FY28.
Unit 6 (IDT, about 5,000 MVA, Vadod adjacent) targeted for operation before December 2026; tank and radiator backward integration (INR170-180 crore) to start in FY27, near Vadod.
capex_capacity: Unit 6 inverter duty transformer facility: about INR65 crore capex, about 5,000 MVA, adjacent to Vadod, targeted operational before end of calendar 2026.
Tank and radiator backward integration: INR170-180 crore capex, robotic, to commence in FY27 near Vadod; benefits expected from FY28.
Capex funded through internal accruals; board has approved a term loan facility that may be drawn if required, with intent to repay in the following year.
Vadod PGCIL approval for up to 400 kV received 2 April 2026, subject to short circuit test and final qualifying requirements; short circuit test transformer to be sent in the coming quarter.
Plans to merge Atlanta Trafo Limited into Atlanta Electricals Limited to be initiated shortly.
demand_pricing: Around 75% of the unexecuted order book is under price variation clause; state utility boards form 60-75% of orders recently, and private long-horizon orders increasingly carry price variation too.
Management says commodity cost increases (copper, aluminium, crude-linked components) are largely passed through; management reports no hit taken in Q4.
Supply constraints persist for OIP bushings; conductor supply improving. Mineral oil shortage in Q4 due to West Asia conflict was managed by prioritising green (ester oil) transformers.
Realisation per MVA rose above INR8 lakh; management expects it to fall as 400/765 kV units (typically 500 MVA) enter.
Three new demand verticals cited: BESS, data centres and renewables. No data centre order in the book yet; BESS orders are in the order book. HVDC not targeted for now.
Competitive landscape: management argues demand will exceed supply for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable given the EHV mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins on 220 kV and below are stable; the gain came from 220 kV scale-up. Margins expected to stay stable going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How is realisation rising from INR7 to INR8 lakh per MVA if EHV will reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-MVA pricing is linked to commodity prices (steel, copper, oil) via customer contracts, so it rises with commodities; it will fall as 500 MVA class 400/765 kV units come in.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for 765 kV and tank/radiator capex and debt drawdown?
qa_highlights.answer: 765 kV is at marketing stage with prototyping this year; orders won this year would be invoiced next year. Tank and radiator facility starts this FY with benefits next year; term loan may be drawn if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Vadod utilisation trajectory and revenue from higher kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation 39% in FY26, 65% in FY27, 100% in FY28; most FY27 output still 220 kV with some 400 kV.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin gap between 400 kV and 220 kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 400/765 kV margins about 200 bps higher; no 400 kV revenue yet.

qa_highlights.question: Data centre order share and HVDC plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No data centre order in the book; management is in talks with customers. HVDC not targeted until 400/765 kV prototypes are validated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of order book on price variation and any Q4 commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the INR2,493 crore order book has price variation; no commodity hit in Q4, and no hit is expected in Q1 as far as management can see.

qa_highlights.question: Margin accretion from backward integration and higher kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration is for supply chain control and quality, not margin; margins expected to remain fairly stable after 400/765 kV development costs.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: 220 kV and below takes 12-18 months; 80-85% of the current order book executes in FY27. Small 400 kV portion delivers from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Transformer demand thumb rule per GW and BESS opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 8-11x transformer capacity per GW generation, expected to tilt higher with BESS; BESS sizing not quantified for Atlanta.

risks_watch: Commodity and input costs: copper, oil and small components (gaskets, paints) are rising; OIP bushing supply is tight.
Working capital will rise to around 80-90 days in FY27-28, which could absorb cash flow.
Execution risk on 400 kV short circuit test, 765 kV tech tie-up (targeted in about two months) and Vadod utilisation ramp to 65%.
Export ramp (15% of revenue target) and first export orders are not yet quantified.
Unit 6 IDT and tank/radiator commissioning timelines (end-CY26 and FY27) could slip.
Management avoided committing to the timing of the short circuit test.
Margins are guided flat, so the margin upside from EHV has not been quantified.
544527|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, capacity and PGCIL approval, with a clear 40% CAGR ambition. Cautious and deliberately non-committal on margin upside, 765 kV timing, export markets and data centre sizing, citing prototype-first discipline.
key_quotes: This margin expansion is structural in nature, driven by operating leverage from higher volumes, a richer product mix tilting towards 220KV class, which now constitutes nearly 52% of our revenue, and improved procurement efficiency on key input materials.
The single biggest operation milestone in the FY26 is the PGCIL approval for the manufacturing of transformers up to 400KV at our unit four, which is Vadod facility.
Team Atlanta booked INR2,507 crores of new order during FY26, which elevated our unexecuted order book on 31st March 2026 to INR2,493 crores.

rows.why: Unit 6 IDT (~5,000 MVA, INR65 cr capex, under construction) targeted before December 2026, and Vadod unit 4 at 39% of its 30,000 MVA nameplate (6,960 MVA produced in ~7 months) is ramping to 65% in FY27 and 100% in FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 40% revenue CAGR, backed by INR2,493 crore unexecuted order book (80-85% executing in FY27) and FY26 output of 22,943 MVA across five units.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Legacy five-unit output of 22,943 MVA in FY26 ran at very high utilisation, management says industry capacity will still fall short, and a INR170-180 cr tank/radiator backward integration is already planned to start in FY27 with a term loan facility approved if needed.

rows.why: Export target set at 15% of revenue within three years, but no export orders quantified yet and first breakthrough only expected in FY27.

rows.why: About 75% of the INR2,493 crore unexecuted order book carries price variation and management reports no commodity hit in Q4 or expected in Q1, so input cost increases are passed through.

544527|2026-06.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore; record order inflow of INR972.42 crore lifted order book to INR3,116.63 crore.
544527|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore, driven mainly by volume from newly commissioned plants, with management saying pricing and product mix were broadly unchanged. Gross margin rose 130 bps to 27.3% and EBITDA margin expanded to 16.5% from 15.5% a year ago, though both moderated from Q4 FY26 seasonally. Order inflow was a record INR972.42 crore, taking the unexecuted order book to about INR3,117 crore, of which about INR2,400 crore is expected to execute in FY27. Management reiterated a 40% revenue CAGR target and a 17-18% margin range, while 400 kV and 765 kV product timelines were pushed out and largely remain conditional.

segments.name: Product mix by voltage class
segments.commentary: 220 kV class was 56% of Q1 revenue, 66 kV class 25%, and 132 kV class about 5.5%. Power transformers were about 79% of revenue, with auto, inverter duty and other products making up the balance.

segments.name: End market
segments.commentary: Transmission and distribution contributed about 66% of revenue and renewable energy about 19%, with thermal power and other industrial making up the rest.

segments.name: Order book by voltage
segments.commentary: 220 kV and above transformers are over 55% of the order book; 400 kV transformers and reactors account for nearly INR275 crore. Management said the entire record Q1 inflow is 220 kV and below.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of 40% YoY growth, applied to FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore (per CFO); management also cited a 40% CAGR for three years.
EBITDA margin expected around 17-18% for the year, with raw material inflation expected to persist but margins sustainable at the Q1 level.
About INR2,400 crore of the ~INR3,100 crore unexecuted order book is due for execution in FY27.
Inverter duty transformer facility (~5,000 MVA) targeted for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Export target of about 15% of revenue within three years; no export revenue in Q1 FY27 and first export execution expected in FY28.
Management expects meaningful revenue from 400 kV transformers from FY28, with 765 kV tech tie-up targeted by end-Q2 FY27 and first 765 kV product by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: B2C - atta
segments.commentary: Volumes declined after West Bengal stopped distributing atta via ration shops in May; NielsenIQ shows packaged atta in West Bengal down 6.3% YoY in the quarter. Displaced local millers now sell unbranded atta in the open market.

segments.name: B2C excluding atta
segments.commentary: Grew 4.9% YoY and 26% QoQ, which management calls the better read of underlying brand demand. E-commerce incl. quick commerce has a FY23-FY26 CAGR above 53%.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue down 13.8% YoY on lower service income and softer core product volumes.

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Revenue grew strongly with margins improving on better realisations. YTD growth about 17-20%; management targets better-than-breakeven and double-digit FY27 growth on a FY26 base of about INR38-40 crore.

segments.name: Sattu
segments.commentary: Volumes grew more than 10% on the back of a Ravindra Jadeja campaign started in April; Bihar and Assam market doubled YoY from a small base.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue from operations expected to decline around 5% on atta pressure.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin expected to improve 50-70 bps YoY, i.e. about 10.5%-11%, per the CFO's clarification.
H2 EBITDA margin structurally lower than H1 because Rabi-crop raw material prices (wheat, gram, spices) firm up from late March/April; advertising to step up in H2.
FY28 margins expected to be similar to FY27 on a conservative basis; new snacks and sweets lines will absorb some of the margin gain.
Hyderabad plant sale (INR325 million, executed 1 October) to yield one-time gain of about INR199 million in Q3 FY27.
Management expects atta volumes to normalise in the medium term; FY28 outlook to be clearer by end of Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Bihar: long-term leased plot in Muzaffarpur from BIADA, possession taken and full amount paid; architect and consultant onboarded; civil work targeted to start around end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Assam: token amount paid for land; legal due diligence done; state approvals in progress; transaction expected post-Diwali.
Capital work in progress of about INR16 crore at September, mainly a sweets and snacks plant near Kolkata (being commissioned) and a bought-out corporate office in Salt Lake to move into next month.

Hyderabad plant (non-core, Johannesburg-based per transcript) sold for INR325 million, about 2.7x net worth; carrying value INR126 million; INR32.2 million advance held as current liability. Proceeds to be redeployed in Eastern India.
Sweets and snacks range (kaju barfi, besan ladoo, soan papdi, ethnic namkeens and bhujiya) to launch first in West Bengal across channels; ready-to-cook and instant mixes in development.
SKUs at 273 versus 253 at end-FY26.
demand_pricing: Competition from unbranded atta sold by displaced flour millers in district markets is the main pressure; management is pursuing counter-strategies started 1 November.
Price hikes depend on competitors; management has enough stock to hold prices for now but will react to wheat price trends.
Earlier spice pricing was aggressive versus local players; management is raising realisations and may take price increases.
Value-added products are 62-65% of revenue this year; value-added margins are above wheat flour and whole wheat flour. Spices margin is above value-added per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for atta volumes and is a price hike likely given the wheat price trend?

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for non-West Bengal regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Onboarding distributors and C&F agents in Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam and Bihar; e-commerce tie-ups in Bihar and Assam; Bihar plant planned for local wheat sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How are spices growing and what is the outlook?

Rising wheat prices and whether competitors move on pricing; no price hike is currently planned.
H2 margin compression from seasonal raw material costs and a stepped-up advertising spend.
Execution timelines for Bihar civil work, the Assam land deal (post-Diwali), and the sweets and snacks launch.
Quality of the one-time gain (INR199 million) in Q3 and the reported cash conversion cycle versus the 32-day level.
B2B weakness (down 13.8% YoY) and a revenue decline of around 5% guided for FY27.

544529|2026-09.headline: Aptus Pharma H1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 48.90 crore from Rs 14.38 crore, with PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore; no forward guidance given.
544529|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 (half-year ended 30 September 2026) revenue from operations of about Rs 48.90 crore versus Rs 14.38 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of about Rs 7.68 crore, PBT of about Rs 6.83 crore and PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore. Management stressed working capital discipline, with inventory of about Rs 16.25 crore and trade receivables of about Rs 28.64 crore against total assets of about Rs 54.55 crore. The strategy was reiterated as three pillars: manufacturing (about 20% of portfolio self-made by March 2028), pan-India expansion (46% geographic coverage by March 2027, pan-India by 2029) and international expansion. Management declined to give any quantitative guidance on revenue, EBITDA, PAT or capex returns during the Q&A.

segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor at about 44% of sales.

segments.name: Chronic and semi-chronic therapy
segments.commentary: About 20% of sales; management said the chronic division was introduced last year and will be strengthened (cardio, diabetes cited).

segments.name: Wellness and OTC

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the vertical is meant to build international opportunities.

Target of 46% geographic coverage across India by March 2027.
Manufacturing expansion targeted by March 2028, with about 20% of the product portfolio made in-house, mainly for self-consumption with the rest for rest-of-world export.
Long-term objective of a pan-India footprint by 2029, with every medical store (cited as over 8.5 lakh) to carry Aptus products.
International expansion to be gradual and opportunity-led in selected markets across Asia, Africa and Latin America.
capex_capacity: Initial manufacturing capex planned at about Rs 35 crore; management said Rs 25 crore will be funded from the ongoing preferential issue, with the rest arranged as needed.
Capex to start only after the exchange grants necessary approval for the preferential issue; a detailed project report has been submitted to authorities.
No commissioning timeline or peak revenue potential from the capex was disclosed.
Company says it will not pursue CDMO; plant is intended for self-consumption and rest-of-world export.
demand_pricing: Portfolio of more than 300 formulations across acute, chronic, wellness and OTC; more than 250 distributors and sub-distributors; retail availability exceeding 45k outlets; more than 10,000 doctors cited as users.
Prescription-led model; management said it is not dependent on a single product and cited diversified portfolio as the key USP.
Field force of 142 on-roll medical representatives, with more than 150 on-roll and off-roll professionals and 200-plus distribution sales representatives; attrition stated below 5-6%.
Gross margins described as good in the pharma industry; no product-level pricing or realisation data given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the guidelines for topline, EBITDA and PAT margin over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not giving any forward figures or guidance on EBITDA, topline or bottom line at present.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's USP versus competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a diversified portfolio across acute, chronic, OTC and wellness, an experienced promoter team, and strong marketing and distribution networks.

qa_highlights.question: Will manufacturing be CDMO or own formulations, and how is the Rs 35 crore capex funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not do CDMO; the plant is for self-consumption (about 20% of products) with the rest for rest-of-world export. Rs 25 crore will come from the preferential issue, with the balance arranged as needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential and completion timeline of the Rs 35 crore capex, and will margins be higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify revenue potential or completion timing, saying it would not give figures now; it said gross margins in pharma are good.

qa_highlights.question: How many marketing employees does the company have and what is attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: 142 on-roll medical representatives, 150-plus on-roll and off-roll professionals and 200-plus distribution sales representatives; attrition below 5-6%.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: receivables of about Rs 28.64 crore are larger than inventory-plus-cash-type buffers suggest against total assets of about Rs 54.55 crore; collection efficiency to be tracked.
Execution risk on manufacturing capex (about Rs 35 crore, Rs 25 crore via preferential issue) with no commissioning timeline or return figures disclosed.
No quantitative guidance, limiting ability to assess sustainability of H1 growth against a low prior-year base of Rs 14.38 crore.
Reliance on third-party WHO-GMP manufacturers for current product supply.
Geographic expansion (46% coverage by March 2027) and international plans lack detail on infrastructure and funding.

544530|2026-03.headline: Anand Rathi Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 125.7% YoY to ₹416 million on revenue of ₹2,557 million, while the MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ.
544530|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 28.1% YoY to ₹2,557 million, with EBITDA up 51.4% to ₹1,103 million (43.2% margin) and PAT up 125.7% to ₹416 million. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 10.2% to ₹9,322 million, EBITDA rose 21.9% to ₹3,796 million, and PAT rose 24.8% to ₹1,293 million. Non-broking income (MTF interest, distribution, other) rose to 53% of the mix in Q4 and 49% for the year, while the MTF book declined from ₹12,317 million in December 2025 to ₹11,019 million in March 2026 due to RBI funding-policy changes and weak markets. Management proposed a ₹5 per share dividend.

segments.name: Broking and related services
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue ₹1,201 million (+14.5% YoY); FY26 ₹4,755 million (-6.8% YoY). FY26 mix: equity cash 51%, F&O 41%, other 8%; Q4 mix: 49%, 41%, 10%.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF, distribution, other)
segments.commentary: MTF book ₹11,019 million with zero NPA and ~61% of exposure from clients with balances below ₹1 crore. Distribution income rose 44.1% in FY26 to ₹1,129 million, spanning MF, PMS, AIF, insurance, bonds, structured products and FDs.

segments.name: Asset management / custody
segments.commentary: AUM ₹77,876 million (+21% YoY); assets under custody ₹944,155 million (+16% YoY). Insurance corporate agency licence obtained in FY26; life and health insurance distribution has started.

guidance_outlook: Target revenue mix of 50:50 between broking and non-broking, with both growing steadily; management said it is not yet happy with the current 51:49 split and expects to reach 50:50 over time.
Management expects non-broking to grow about 40-45% annually for the first few years, and broking about 15% a year.
Overall revenue growth aim of about 15-20% YoY.
Earlier guidance of an MTF book of ₹15,000 million by FY26 was missed; the book ended at ₹11,019 million.
Debt-equity ceiling set at a maximum of 1.5x; current ratio is about 0.6x.
capex_capacity: MTF book contracted 10.53% QoQ in Q4 FY26 after RBI policy changes narrowed bank and NBFC funding avenues for capital market intermediaries; management said the company had to control growth and preserve cash for margin requirements.
Management said the RBI funding-related deferral was postponed to another quarter, and expects to resume MTF growth as funding routes reopen.
IPO completed in September 2025 raising ₹745 crore, used mainly for working capital.
Stock basket for MTF restricted internally to fewer than 1,000 stocks versus about 2,000+ permitted by the regulator; internal margins set above exchange margins for many stocks.
Branch network and business partner expansion planned in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.
demand_pricing: Market backdrop: Nifty fell about 15% in Q4 FY26 and the company described a consolidation phase, FII outflows and West Asia-related volatility; clients became cautious on new and existing positions.
Demat accounts rose from 15.14 crore (Mar 2024) to 22.2 crore (Feb 2026); mutual fund AUM about ₹82.02 lakh crore (Feb 2026), up 24.8% YoY.
Active client base was flat to down 2-3% in FY26, while total client base grew 12.7% (corrected from 12%).
MTF yields: management said no significant pricing pressure yet despite competitor entry, with low MTF penetration among its clients; it did not rule out yield changes.
About 42% of active clients have been with the company for over five years; 83% of active clients are over 30 years old; about 60% of broking clients use the digital platform.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company guide broking and wealth management over coming quarters (client acquisition, advisory, digital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth management sits in a separate group company; this entity focuses on broking and distribution, with a phygital model and about 60% of broking clients on the digital platform.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage risks in broking and advisory (volatility, compliance, credit) while keeping profitability stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited restricting the MTF basket to under 1,000 stocks, higher-than-exchange margins, zero MTF NPA over eight-plus years, QSB broker status and a debt-equity ceiling of 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: How should the 50:50 broking/non-broking mix evolve over the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects non-broking to grow 40-45% a year and broking about 15%, with overall revenue growth of 15-20% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Are MTF spreads sustainable amid new competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not facing much pressure yet due to pent-up demand and low utilisation; yields may change but it aims to maintain current levels, with growth gated by capital and funding.

qa_highlights.question: How much of broking is derivatives vs cash, and what is the STT impact? What is exposure to the RBI proprietary-trading rule?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue split is about 50:50 cash vs derivatives, with focus on hedged and investment-led F&O and commodity trades. The company said it has no proprietary book, so the RBI prop-book rule does not affect it. The STT impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How much of AUC growth came from new clients vs existing clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AUC growth came mainly from existing clients, with the total client base up 12.7% and active clients flat to down 2-3% in FY26.

risks_watch: MTF book contraction (down 10.53% QoQ) and dependence on bank/NBFC funding under RBI rules; watch the funding reopening and the ₹15,000 million target.
Broking revenue fell 6.8% in FY26 with active clients flat to down, and F&O is 41% of the mix; the sensitivity to market cycles and STT changes is not quantified.
Competition in MTF could pressure yields; management said it is not yet seeing it.
Q4 PAT (+125.7%) may not be a clean run-rate given the quarterly volatility; watch whether margins hold when markets are weak.
Growth in non-broking (40-45%) and broking (~15%) is aspirational, given FY26 broking was down.

we closed the year with zero NPA in the portfolio, reflecting our continuous underwriting standards and strong focus on asset quality.

544530|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.37% YoY to ₹2,461 million, but PAT after a ₹209.96 million exceptional fraud charge was ₹233.51 million (+2.35% YoY).
544530|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 22.37% YoY to about ₹2,461 million, with EBITDA up 30.19% to ₹973 million at a 39.54% margin. PAT before exceptional items rose about 71% to ₹391 million, but a ₹209.96 million exceptional charge for restoring securities to two dormant depository clients cut reported PAT to ₹233.51 million. MTF book reached ₹13,318 million (+55% YoY) and distribution AUM ₹94,791 million (+25.82% YoY). Management guided MTF to ₹1,750–1,800 crores and distribution AUM up 40% by year-end FY27.

segments.name: Broking
segments.commentary: Contributed 52% of revenue; broking income ₹1,280 million, up about 7% QoQ, with 51% of it from equity cash, the core focus area.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF + distribution)
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue; MTF interest income ₹428 million and distribution income ₹275 million. Distribution income dipped QoQ, which management attributed to seasonally lower insurance sales in April–June.

segments.name: Employees
segments.commentary: Headcount 2,263 versus 2,148 in Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: MTF book expected at ₹1,750–1,800 crores by end of FY27, from ₹1,330 crores currently.
Distribution AUM targeted to grow about 40%, driven by higher wallet share of existing clients.
Continue to target a near 50:50 broking to non-broking income mix over the medium term.
Long-term revenue growth band of 15–25% (typically 20–25%); PAT growth target of around 30–35% while the mix is not yet 50:50.
Planned Dubai subsidiary to serve UAE-based NRI clients, subject to licences; board has passed a resolution.
Management expects borrowings to rise to lift the debt-equity ratio, which it sees as comfortable at around 2x versus industry 1.5–2x.
capex_capacity: MTF book rose from about ₹1,100 crores at the March 2026 trough to ₹1,330 crores, with growth continuing in Q1.
Management said borrowing is being used to fund working capital and MTF; it expects leverage to rise from 0.81x.
Credit rating upgraded: short-term bank facilities to A1+, long-term to A+.
Dubai subsidiary planned for NRI servicing; a GIFT City subsidiary already exists and is active for NRI business.
demand_pricing: Cash market turnover rose about 13% QoQ, while derivatives activity moderated after SEBI measures (upfront option premium, expiry-day margins, higher contract sizes, weekly expiry rationalisation).
RBI revised capital market exposure framework effective 1 July 2026 is expected to raise bank working-capital costs for broking intermediaries.
MTF yield about 14%; management said spreads depend on market liquidity and borrowing costs, which are currently higher.
Demat accounts reached 23 crore in June; SIP additions about 66 lakh in June versus 53 lakh in March; 42 companies filed draft offer documents with SEBI in the quarter.

Distribution revenue in April–June fell QoQ because insurance sales are concentrated in January–March; mutual fund and other AUM grew QoQ and the company recorded its highest net collections in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MTF interest income flat despite about 21% book growth, and is MTF pricing falling?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said projects have been funded through internal accrual and project debt, with equity not ruled out at company level. JV equity is 50% of 25% of INR 320-340 crore (about INR 40 crore for True Colors), which management said can come from internal accrual or bank debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising faster than revenue, and what is being done?

qa_highlights.question: What margin does each business line earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated EBITDA is about 17%, in a 14-18% band; consumables, ink, paper and printing run at similar margins, with machines the lowest margin (about 5% of gross margin). Segment-level margins were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why move into base paper manufacturing, which is a commodity business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV targets ultra-low 29 GSM specialty sublimation media, not commodity base paper, because Indian mills cannot produce below 32 GSM. It said the output is for the company's ecosystem and not for paper mills.

qa_highlights.question: How much of INKIA's output goes to True Colors, and can INKIA's financials be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35-40% of INKIA's output went to the True Colors ecosystem last year, with the rest sold to other distributors; ecosystem consumption averages 115 tons/month. INKIA standalone H1 numbers were not shared pending regulatory confirmation.

qa_highlights.question: What valuation was used for the INKIA merger share swap?

544532|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 235% YoY to INR591 crore, but EBITDA margin was 12.1% and FY26 PAT margin 8.5%, below the 11% promised earlier.
544532|2026-03.overview: Solarworld reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR591 crore (up 235% YoY), EBITDA of INR73 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of INR49 crore (8.1% net margin). For FY26, total income was INR1,416 crore (up 1.57% YoY), EBITDA INR187.9 crore (13.3%) and PAT INR120.4 crore (8.5%). Management blamed a loss-making initial module ramp after ALMM approval in December 2025 and sharp raw material cost increases in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict. The company is pivoting toward BESS, with a 582 MWac / 1.2 GWh DC BESS project pipeline and a 3.4 GW BESS line in trials.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC revenue about INR1,250 crore; management cites EPC PAT margin close to 10.5%. EPC margin guided at 9-11% through the cycle and 8-11% overall for FY27. Solar EPC order book about INR1,674 crore.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 BESS revenue was nil; management guides INR800-1,000 crore in FY27. BESS order book about INR1,136 crore. Q4 orders from NTPC at Solapur and Unchahar aggregate about 514 MWh, order value about INR5 billion incl. O&M. BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT.

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW Roorkee module line began operations after ALMM approval in December 2025; about two to two-and-a-half months of run-time in FY26 produced a slight loss. Breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; FY26-27 utilisation expected at 40-45% on about 600 MW captive NTPC REL orders, rising to 60-65% with more orders. Line capex about INR146 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order book conversion target at least 70% of about INR2,800 crore, i.e. about INR2,000 crore revenue; EPC about INR2,000 crore including BESS INR800-1,000 crore.
Management expects 40-45% revenue growth in FY27 and says it will not sustain FY26's 200-250% growth.
Overall EBITDA/PAT margin guided at 8-11%; sustaining current margins if the West Asia conflict eases, with slight downside if raw material prices keep rising.
BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT; 3.4 GW BESS line capex about INR55-60 crore, potential revenue about INR3,000 crore at full capacity (740 containers at INR4.5 crore each).
Q1 and Q2 seasonally weak; Q3 and Q4 strong. Management declined to give a half-yearly split.
1.2 GW solar cell line at Pandhurna targeted for commercial operation by June 2027; cell-line funds to be deployed from Q3 FY27.
No near-term plans to add module or cell capacity until about 75-80% captive utilisation is visible.

BESS: 3.4 GW fully automated line (KUKA robotics) ready, trials underway; capex about INR55-60 crore already spent.
Solar cell: 1.2 GW line at Pandhurna, approvals mostly received, construction to start around June 2026, commercial operation targeted by June 2027.
Junction box: 5 GW line being set up in a joint venture; site ready for trials.

Operational capacity to be added on commissioning: a 272 MW project and a 70 MW project expected to complete in June 2026; management expects about 600 MW near term, about 700 MW next quarter and about 1.5 GW by year-end.
demand_pricing: PSU tenders were about 40 GW last year; the company executes about 1-1.5 GW a year, so it sees limited impact from a slower tendering market.
Raw material costs up sharply since Oct 2025: copper about +40%, aluminium about +50%, steel higher; INR depreciated from about 85-86 to about 96 per USD, affecting BESS imported inputs.
ALMM List-II (cells) applies from June 2026; management expects 90-95% of projects to shift to DCR cells, with a possible 6-12 month cell shortage.
Current order book has no ALMM-2 cell requirement, giving a headway of about a year. Lithium cells for BESS are sourced from China as no Indian supplier exists.
PPA signing delays after L1 bids and grid connectivity constraints are slowing the solar tender market; management expects connectivity to take 10-12 more months to resolve.
Claims filed with SJVN for about INR219 crore; only INR52 crore recognised as receivable. Ind AS allows recognition only after dispute-board award.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin is 8-8.5% versus the 11% promised earlier, and top line is short of the INR1,500 crore target. What is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC PAT margin is about 10.5%, with the module loss from a short ramp and Q4 raw material headwinds dragging the total. Guidance is INR1,900-2,000 crore revenue and 8-11% overall margins.

qa_highlights.question: Battery cell unit timeline, and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1.2 GW cell line at Pandhurna is now targeted for commercial start by June 2027, with construction starting around June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expense rise, and what is the BESS capex and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expense rose to INR83 million from INR74 million; last year's base included a INR140 million write-off that was recovered this year. The 3.4 GW BESS line capex is INR55-60 crore; margin 14-15% PBT.

qa_highlights.question: How will the module line utilisation ramp, and what is breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is around 30-35% utilisation. Utilisation should reach 40-45% on existing NTPC REL orders (about 600 MW), rising to 60-65% with new orders. All existing EPC orders can be serviced in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand module or cell capacity, and why are PPAs being rescinded?
qa_highlights.answer: No expansion planned until 75-80% captive use is visible. PPA delays stem from DISCOM absorption and transmission constraints; management expects resolution by around end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ROW, labour and the EPC tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: ROW compensation is moving to market rates, which helps, but management does not see it as the biggest hurdle; no major labour issues. Tender activity is slower, but the company's order book is full.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from copper, aluminium, steel and INR depreciation; management guides 8-11% overall margin range.

544532|2026-09.headline: Solarworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 77% YoY to Rs 2,244 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.9% and management now targets 6-7% for FY27.
544532|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was reported as Rs 2,244 crore (transcript figure, likely a transcription error for a much smaller base), up about 77% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 15.2 crore (5.9% margin) versus Rs 18.1 crore a year earlier. Half-year revenue was Rs 412 crore (about 100% YoY) with H1 EBITDA of Rs 35.8 crore (8.3%) and PAT of Rs 13.7 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to metal price spikes on fixed-price PSU contracts won before the spike, with LOAs delayed by 4-5 months. Order book stood at Rs 3,856 crore as of October 31, 2026, with BESS contributing about Rs 1,138 crore.

segments.name: Solar ETC and O&M

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW ALMM-listed module plant is operational; 5 GW junction box line has commenced operation. Management expects 60-70% internal utilisation of the planned solar cell capacity.

segments.name: Solar cell JV (Madhya Pradesh)
segments.commentary: 2.4 GW TOPCon cell facility at Narmadapuram via JV; targeted commercial production June 2027 (management also said second quarter of next year). First equity tranche of about Rs 26.8 crore paid on October 30, 2026.

Management said the board will return to shareholders in the current quarter with short-term actions on shareholder value; buyback was raised by an investor and not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Profitability roadmap for the next 12 months, 2 years and 3 years, and revised PAT guidance versus earlier IPO-stage guidance of Rs 200-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: BESS margins at EBITDA and PAT level.

qa_highlights.question: Why annual report disclosure on procurement/pass-through differs from the guided margin cut from 10.5% to 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in achieving FY27 guidance, given H1 revenue of Rs 1,369 crore (as stated in call) and guidance of Rs 1,600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is typically much stronger (H2 FY26 about Rs 100 crore against H1 about Rs 20 crore as stated) and it is fairly confident of meeting the revenue and margin targets.

qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon technology; 70-80% of capacity to be used internally (60-70% per a later answer) and 15-20% to be sold externally; management said it remains asset-light and will not scale manufacturing beyond ETC needs.

544544|2026-09.headline: Telge Projects FY26 revenue rose about 57% to Rs 40.2 crore with Q4 EBITDA margin of 35%; order book stands at Rs 25 crore.
544544|2026-09.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 40.2 crore (up about 57% from Rs 25.6 crore), with EBITDA of Rs 9.55 crore (24% margin) and PAT of Rs 5.9 crore (15% margin). Q4 revenue was Rs 14.4 crore (up 13.7% YoY, about 58% QoQ), with Q4 EBITDA of Rs 5 crore (35%) and PAT of Rs 3.3 crore (23%). Management said the current active order book is about Rs 25 crore, with a further Rs 6 crore in bidding, and guided to a 60-70% revenue CAGR and to maintaining Q4-level margins. Much of the answers were qualitative, and several figures were inconsistent or only partly answered.

segments.name: Standalone India (structural, BIM, steel and precast detailing)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue grew about 22% YoY per the analyst's reading of the numbers, against about 60% consolidated growth. Management said the US subsidiaries handle sales and client relations while execution sits in the parent in India, so the entities cannot be cleanly separated.

segments.name: US subsidiaries (Midwest, Draftco, Edward Farr Architects)
segments.commentary: Edward Farr was acquired on 3 March and consolidated for about one month (about Rs 1.5 crore revenue, about Rs 40 lakh PAT). Edward Farr had CY2025 revenue of about Rs 14 crore and PAT margin of 10-12%, and was bought at 2.5x EBITDA. Management said about Rs 10 crore of the Rs 25 crore order book relates to the architecture business.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue CAGR of 60-70%, with FY27 cited as the first year, though no absolute FY27 revenue figure was given.
Management aims to keep EBITDA and PAT margins at Q4 levels (EBITDA about 35%, PAT 20-23%) in FY27 and said it will not go below that.

US billing rates are targeted at $45-60 per hour, up from $25-35 per hour previously.

capex_capacity: Nashik office became operational during FY26 and the Nashik team was expanded; Latur branch was added over the last 2-3 years.

IPO proceeds: about Rs 7 crore utilised so far. Management said the office-premises object was deviated from, leaving Rs 5 crore for acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Order book is about Rs 25 crore (about 80% US), and a pipeline of about Rs 6 crore is at the RFQ or bidding stage, expected to convert within 2 weeks to a month.
Order book has been adding about Rs 4-5 crore per month over the last year, per management.
About 20 new clients were added in Q4, all from the US. Total customer count for FY26 was 96.

Seasonality: Q2 is the slowest quarter; Q4 is typically strongest.
Attrition in India is about 10% per management; subsidiary attrition is zero.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach 60-70% CAGR, and what is the go-to-market and visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book builds through the year and the Rs 6 crore RFQ pipeline is short-term. Cross-selling with Edward Farr and a higher ticket size (Rs 8-10 crore) are the longer-term drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 growth organic or inorganic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the acquisition closed on 3 March, so only one month was consolidated. Subsidiaries are now counted as organic growth, and inorganic growth will come from new acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 73 to 108?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most receivables are due in 30-45 days and that the major part of the balance is with a related party. Collections were accelerated in April and May, and DSO is now about 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why can EBITDA margin hold at 30-35% when peers run about 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited US-based teams that help secure higher billing rates ($45-60/hour target), expansion into lower-cost regions such as Nashik and Latur, and AI-led productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of recurring revenue and project duration?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing clients contribute 60-70% of revenue. Project duration varies from one month to a couple of years, and larger Rs 8-10 crore projects are expected to run longer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 costs rose on deliberate leadership and business-development hires. No new leadership hires are planned for FY27, so growth in employee cost should be lower.

Full-year FY27 revenue of 60-70% growth implies about Rs 64-68 crore, which is not yet covered by the Rs 25 crore order book; the analyst questioned the visibility.

AI-driven commoditisation of BIM modelling work could affect pricing; management did not give a specific response on this risk.

544545|2026-03.headline: TruAlt FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR1,704 crore and PAT to INR80.26 crore as OMC ethanol allocation was cut to about 34% of bids.
544545|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: ethanol tender allocation was cut to about 26 crore litres against a 72 crore litre bid, and private OMCs sought to revise prices on purchase orders already issued at about INR60 per litre. Standalone revenue fell about 9% to INR1,704 crore, while EBITDA margin rose to 19.81% from 18.98%. PAT fell to INR80.26 crore from INR140 crore, driven by depreciation (up to INR84 crore) after three dual-feed plants were capitalised, higher finance cost (INR157.85 crore) and deferred tax. Management is relying on a pending 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation, plus SAF, CBG and fuel-retail expansion for growth.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 ethanol sales about 24-26 crore litres (about 3 crore litres ENA) at average realisation of about INR67 per litre; OMC allocation was about 26 crore litres vs 72 crore litre bid. Current sales run rate about 2.2 crore litres per month vs 5.5-6 crore litre capacity.

segments.name: Compressed Biogas (CBG)
segments.commentary: First plant (10 TPD) generates about INR42 crore revenue at 85%+ utilisation; Sumitomo JV (TruAlt Gas, 49% partner) plans three 20 TPD plants and GAIL JV (Leafiniti, 49%) plans six plants of 12 TPD, targeting 162 TPD gross by Q4 FY27. Management guides about 50% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Fuel retail
segments.commentary: Seven franchise outlets operating with zero capex, generating about INR100-105 crore revenue and about 5% EBITDA; target of 11 outlets near term and 87 total (11 plus 76 shortlisted) subject to crude stabilisation.

segments.name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)
segments.commentary: Planned 10 crore litre per annum plant in Andhra Pradesh (MoU signed); Honeywell UOP technology transfer agreement signed; FID awaits long-term offtake contract and pricing. Plans to divert about 20 crore litres of ethanol capacity to SAF.

segments.name: DDGS (by-product, within ethanol)
segments.commentary: DDGS revenue about INR28 crore in FY26, at base price about INR24 per kg; operations were mostly on syrup in Q3 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ethanol volume target of at least 40 crore litres, with 55 crore litres if the pending 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation is implemented; management declined to give a revenue figure.

Management expects the 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation to be implemented by about September 2026 (H1 FY27), dependent on the Supreme Court LTOA matter being disposed of; courts resume about 3 June.

CBG: three TruAlt Gas plants (Sumitomo) and six Leafiniti plants (GAIL) to be commissioned by Q4 FY27, bringing gross capacity to about 162 TPD; EPC tenders for Leafiniti to be floated in early June 2026.
Fuel retail: 76 shortlisted outlets to be fast-tracked once crude prices stabilise, with total count above 90 by next financial year (earlier stated 87 by year-end).
Management says the INR150 crore PMG1 subsidy approval is at the final Secretary-level committee; receipt is linked to plant commissioning, expected in 24-30 months (FY29).
Management says no additional capex is planned beyond the capitalised dual-feed plants, but CBG and SAF expansions are in progress.
capex_capacity: Five ethanol plants fully commissioned; three of five converted to dual-feed (maize/broken rice), with more than INR400 crore capitalised, driving higher depreciation.

Ethanol capacity about 55-60 crore litres on 300-330 operating days; management targets syrup operation for about 100 days in the crushing season and 200-230 days on alternative grains for dual-feed units.
CBG: current 10 TPD operating; TruAlt Gas building three 20 TPD plants; Leafiniti targets six 12 TPD plants with six sites identified and land procurement advanced.
CBG funding is a 70:30 debt-to-equity mix; Sumitomo debt tied up with NABARD at 8.65%, and Leafiniti has four or five sanctions at lower rates.
SAF: land identified in Andhra Pradesh near a seaport; FID to follow a long-term offtake contract.
demand_pricing: Average ethanol sales realisation about INR67 per litre; ENA realisation about INR62 per litre; ENA market price fell from an expected INR62-63 to about INR55-56 per litre.
Public sector OMC contract prices: maize-based INR71, syrup-based INR65, damaged grains INR64, B-heavy molasses INR60, FCI rice INR58, C-heavy molasses INR58.
Private OMCs (8 crore litres allocated) requested price revision from about INR60 per litre; only about 1.6 crore litres lifted so far, with 6.2 crore litres still pending.
Court order (4 February 2026) values the pending 15.62 crore litres at about INR1,062 crore; management states inventory of about INR460-500 crore is built up.
CBG billed at about INR84-85 per kg; rumoured Sampoorn policy could lift gas price to INR100 and add INR5 per kg PLI (unconfirmed by management).
Management cites a blending increase from 20% to 21% (notified), with E22/E27/E30 BIS standards and E85/E100 notified; each 1% blending adds about 55-56 crore litres of demand.

qa_highlights.question: What was total FY26 ethanol volume and when did the allocation change happen?
qa_highlights.answer: About 24 crore litres sold versus 30 crore litres of tender allocation; management said the mechanism had not changed, but the 15 crore litre court-ordered carry-forward was not implemented.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 15 crore litre court order be implemented?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes for implementation by September or H1 FY27, after the court-pending LTOA matter is disposed of; the OMCs were past the 90-day period set by the 4 February order.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics of ethanol, PLI and interest subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of about INR68.28 crore; Karnataka PLI at 1.75% of turnover; interest subvention up to 50% of term-loan interest capped at 6% per annum, per CFO explanation.

qa_highlights.question: How will CBG be funded and sourced?
qa_highlights.answer: 70:30 debt-equity; Sumitomo plants sourced from TruAlt's own spent wash and press mud; GAIL plants sourced from the open market, with at least three times raw material within 20 km of each site.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about 21 days (realised in 15-17 days on average); payables up to about 60 days; net working capital about 40 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the feedstock split?
qa_highlights.answer: Group companies supplied under 55% of FY26 feedstock; over 45% was sourced from the open market, with the share from non-group sources expected to rise.

risks_watch: Pending 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation has not been implemented; timing depends on the Supreme Court LTOA matter and OMC compliance.
Private OMCs (8 crore litres) have sought price revision from about INR60 per litre; 6.2 crore litres still unlifted, and ENA prices have fallen to about INR55-56 per litre.
Higher depreciation and finance cost are compressing PBT and PAT, with standalone PAT down about 43%.
CBG expansion depends on the Sampoorn policy (rumoured, not notified) and on the Sumitomo land dispute that cut one plant from four to three.
Retail expansion (76 outlets) is paused due to crude price volatility; SAF FID awaits an offtake contract and pricing.
Standalone inventory of about INR460-500 crore is unsold and needs liquidation in FY27.

Management guided to 11-12 crore litres of sales in Q2 and about 44 crore litres of orders on hand for FY27, but flagged that maize prices at around INR25.5/kg have compressed margins, so earnings depend on inventory bought at lower prices. Several analyst answers were qualified by poor line quality and some questions went unanswered.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk from sugar companies adding ethanol capacity?

544545|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 606% YoY to INR811 crore and PAT turned to INR35 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.03% on maize prices up 25-30%.
544545|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR811 crore versus INR115 crore a year earlier, and up from INR627 crore in Q1, with PAT of about INR35 crore against a loss of INR38 crore. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.03% from a higher H1 level of about 18.2%, as maize prices rose 25-30% during the quarter and raw material was bought at elevated cost. Ethanol allocations were increased during the quarter after a Supreme Court judgment, lifting the last supply year's allocation from 24.5 crore litres to 34.5 crore litres, with a further 5 crore litres reported. Management guided to a shrinking bottom line in the coming year due to El Nino-linked feedstock shortages, while CBG capacity is being added.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Ethanol volumes sold were 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres in H1). About 8.5 crore litres of orders remain to be supplied in October-November, and management expects 6-7 crore litres of additional volume in November-December.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas)
segments.commentary: First 20 TPD JV plant with Sumitomo is ramping up; two more plants are expected in the quarter, taking installed capacity to about 72 TPD from four operating plants. Management expects about INR20 crore of CBG revenue from the two to three plants over the next two quarters.

segments.name: SAF (sustainable aviation fuel)
segments.commentary: Front-end engineering is ongoing and about INR150 crore of viability gap funding has been received under PM JI-VAN for the proposed plant. Capex awaits a government roadmap that has not yet been announced.

segments.name: Fuel retail
segments.commentary: About 7 outlets are operational with more nearing commissioning; outlet expansion is being slowed due to crude price volatility.

guidance_outlook: Ethanol capacity utilisation expected to rise to at least 75-80% on average, from 65-70% in the last supply year; new-year allocation expected at about 40-42 crore litres (one analyst question cited 45 crore litres as the expectation).

Ethanol EBITDA margin expected to dip about 1-2 percentage points on average versus the run-rate once new tenders are allocated; Q2 described as the seasonally weakest quarter, with margin recovery expected from Q3.
Management expects the bottom line to shrink due to El Nino-linked raw material price and availability pressure; intends to forward-buy and stock maize and rice.
Raw material cost as a share of revenue expected to be sub-70% going forward, versus 62-66% historically.
Ethanol gross margin currently about 30% per CFO, which management declined to guide forward.

CBG: expected capex of about INR300 crore for four to five add-on plants at about INR65 crore per plant, with incremental term debt of about INR70-80 crore; GOBARdhan subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD (25% currently receivable) and about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

Badami (Unit 5) slump sale expected to realise about INR170 crore, with about INR125-130 crore of term loan repaid and about INR40-46 crore retained; management expects about INR22 crore annual cost savings.
capex_capacity: Ethanol installed capacity about 2,000 KLPD (about 1,900 crore litres per year industry view); management says all ethanol capex is complete and no ethanol capex is planned next quarter. Three plants converted to grain-based dual feed; one 400 KLPD plant to run on C-heavy molasses/ENA.
Ethanol capacity utilisation was 62% in Q2 at the 400 KLPD plant and about 64-65% in H1.
CBG installed capacity to reach about 72 TPD by end of quarter; plan to start construction of six additional units with GAIL.
Srikakulam SAF plant planned on the PM JI-VAN grant; capex to start only after the government roadmap is announced.
Expected Q3 CBG working capital requirement of about INR25-30 crore at 100 TPD scale; current 10 TPD plant needs about INR2.5-3 crore.
demand_pricing: Maize prices rose 25-30% in Q2; management expects maize availability down about 35% and rice and sugarcane down 10-12% next year due to El Nino.
Ethanol realisation this year: maize-based about INR68/litre, damaged food grain about INR64, FCI rice about INR60; blended average about INR64-65 versus about INR67 last year.
Government reduced maize-based ethanol price by about INR3/litre in the current tender; sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses banned for the 2026-27 supply year.
ENA long-contract prices about INR62-63/litre, with ENA production cost about INR1.5-2/litre lower than ethanol from C-heavy molasses.
DDGS byproduct price about INR26-30/kg. CBG revenue per TPD about INR4-4.5 crore; gas price rises from INR84 to about INR104/kg (up to INR116-120/kg for higher purity) under GOBARdhan 2.0.
Management sees roughly 230 mono-feed sugar-based plants out of about 500 unable to supply continuous ethanol, and the OMC tender demand about 1,100 crore litres.

Chemical/industrial alcohol demand cited at 250-300 crore litres; management expects 40-50% to be met by Indian producers. Industrial alcohol imports (RS) now INR58-60/litre versus INR47-48 previously.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance for next two quarters, and what execution risks for the Srikakulam SAF plant and feedstock strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8.5 crore litres of existing orders for October-November; new-year allocation expected at 40-42 crore litres, subject to bids. Feedstock to be sourced nationally (Bihar, MP, Punjab) with warehouses being secured.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans, and working capital risk from CBG expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No ethanol capex; CBG capex about INR300 crore for four to five plants with about INR70-80 crore new term debt. Working capital need is minimal; CBG subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD reduces term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol volumes this quarter, and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol sold: 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres H1). Margin expected to rise from Q3 with a possible 1-2 point average dip once tenders are allocated.

qa_highlights.question: CBG revenue ramp and subsidy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore CBG revenue expected over the next two quarters from two to three plants; subsidy of about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and raw material cost structure for ethanol and CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize ethanol about INR68/litre, blended about INR64-65; raw material share below 70% of revenue. CBG EBITDA guided at about 50-55% at 20 TPD, against a track record near 60%; revenue about INR80 crore per 20 TPD plant.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory holding and margin sustainability in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of INR206 crore at September is expected to clear with the new season. Management would not disclose the maize-based realisation for next year before allocations; about 4.5 crore litres remain to be supplied this quarter.

risks_watch: Maize and raw material price inflation and feedstock availability with El Nino; management expects a squeeze on the bottom line in the next supply year.
Ethanol price cut in the current OMC tender (about INR3/litre) and allocation outcome for 40-42 crore litres, not yet confirmed.
SAF project depends on an unannounced government roadmap; no capex has started.
Finance costs rose to INR87 crore in H1 (from INR76 crore), and debt-to-equity is about 0.55x; new CBG term debt of about INR70-80 crore is planned.
Promoter pledge and share purchase intent (stake about 71%, headroom to 75%) and a personal loan were raised in the call; management said it does not affect the company.
Subsidy receipt timing (INR25-30 crore expected by December or January) and the Badami slump sale completion.

Management was evasive on forward ethanol margin and realisation numbers, saying these depend on allocations, and it deflected a question on promoter personal financing.
