544546|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 42.5% to INR84.22 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 17% and PAT margin to 10.9% as spending on talent, platform and new verticals rose.
544546|2026-03.overview: Chatterbox Technologies held its maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), its first since its IPO. Revenue from operations grew 42.5% YoY to INR84.22 crores, and EBITDA and PAT rose in absolute terms to INR14.32 crores and INR9.2 crores. Margins moderated, which management attributed to investment in talent, platform capabilities and new verticals. Management declined to give formal guidance, though it said FY27 net margins would be similar to FY26 with an aim to expand them. Several questions focused on the sharp fall in market cap after listing, the possibility of a QYOU Media merger, the delayed results timeline, and the AAGE edutainment app; management answered most of these qualitatively or deferred them.

segments.name: Chatterbox Represent (exclusive talent management)
segments.commentary: Contributed 39.27% of FY26 revenue, the largest vertical. Management said margins are fixed but absolute contribution can grow as exclusive creators are added; it manages over 100 creators exclusively.

segments.name: Brand Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 36.18% of FY26 revenue. No separate growth or margin commentary was given in the call.

segments.name: ChtrSocial
segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

guidance_outlook: No formal financial guidance given. Management said the opportunity ahead is significantly larger and it remains optimistic on healthy medium- to long-term growth.
FY27 net margin expected to be similar to FY26 (about 10%); management said it is aiming higher and streamlining opex.
ChtrSocial expected to at least double its revenue in the upcoming period; no percentage target given.
AAGE edutainment app launch targeted within FY27 after development was paused for the IPO; it is still at the UX/UI stage with focus-group validation planned.
Management said integrated benefits from QYOU Media collaboration will become more visible in H2 2026.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets roughly doubled, while intangible assets under development stayed at INR4.68 crores; the AAGE app was on hold during the IPO and is being resumed.
Chtr Studios (video production) and Dubai subsidiary were established; the Dubai subsidiary is not 100% owned by Chatterbox (reason asked but not clearly answered in the call).
No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management said growth came from a mix of higher ticket sizes, organic growth across verticals, new client wins and international expansion, with an equal-mix view endorsed by the analyst.
Over 500 brands served, more than 2,000 campaigns executed, and a team of over 100 professionals, per management.
Management does not disclose net revenue retention, but said a significant part of growth came from existing enterprise clients with larger mandates and cross-selling of ChtrSocial and Studios.
Creator economy said to grow at a 25-30% CAGR globally, and BCG estimate cited of over USD 1 trillion annual creator-economy spend by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals will drive growth over the next 2-3 years, and will ChtrSocial, Represent, international or technology lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come from multiple engines: ChtrSocial, technology/AI platform, exclusive talent management and international (MENA first, then APAC and LATAM). No percentage targets were given.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments have the highest margins and where is operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Farrel Arora said ChtrSocial and the production arm (Studios) have the highest margin contribution. Represent is scalable in absolute rupee terms but its margins are fixed.

qa_highlights.question: Why has intangible assets under development stayed flat at INR4.68 crores, and what is the AAGE app?
qa_highlights.answer: AAGE was put on hold during the IPO. It is an edutainment app mixing short-form video, learning and gamification with AI; launch is targeted within FY27 after UX/UI curation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR26 crore trade receivables is not yet due?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR17.5 crores is within the standard 60-day credit period. Management said collections usually realise in 60-90 days (around 70-75 days on average), and most of the not-due amount should now be realised.

qa_highlights.question: Did volume growth come from more campaigns, new clients or deeper wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix of all three, with deeper wallet share from existing clients and international efforts contributing; no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the reasons behind the Dubai subsidiary not being 100% owned, the top-five customers, and whether QYOU Media will merge with Chatterbox at a market cap of INR78 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Curt Marvis declined to comment on any merger, saying only that the company is always looking at ways to increase shareholder value and that a public vehicle enables accretive M&A. Top-five customer data and the Dubai ownership reason were not answered directly in the call.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin 17% and PAT margin 10.9% in FY26, with FY27 PAT margin guided at similar levels (about 10%). Watch whether opex is streamlined.
Receivables: INR26 crores of trade receivables at March 2026 against INR84.22 crores revenue. Track receivable days and cash conversion next quarter.
Results disclosure timing: results were announced on 29 May, with the investor presentation and call later, and a family matter was cited as the cause. Investor-relations sentiment was questioned.

Related-party and governance questions: the parent QYOU Media (listed in Canada/US) merger was raised but not addressed; the Dubai subsidiary ownership and the market-cap decline post-listing (analyst cited about INR78 crores vs about INR160 crores at debut) remain open.
Customer concentration: top-five customer contribution was asked for but not disclosed.
AAGE app launch in FY27 and its monetisation are unproven; management said it will validate the model first.

544547|2026-03.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.
544547|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly standalone and consolidated revenue in company history, with standalone revenue up 89% YoY to INR133 crore and consolidated at INR192 crore. Full-year standalone revenue grew 48% to INR313 crore, but standalone PAT was INR12.44 crore and consolidated PAT was INR12.76 crore, with management attributing the margin pressure to freight and geopolitical logistics costs, HexL brand investment and higher employee costs. Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

segments.commentary: Customised machines of other brands contributed about 62%, refurbished used construction equipment about 35%, and HexL own-brand about 5% (4.9-5% consolidated; about 7% standalone).

segments.name: Geography FY26
segments.commentary: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each (per management's approximate figures), with the rest in single digits. Management said exports are about 97-98% of revenue.

segments.commentary: Own brand in early build-out with lower margins; management targets 11-12% of FY27 revenue and about 150 units in FY27.

demand_pricing: Management said demand for construction and mining equipment stayed resilient, supported by infrastructure, industrial capex and replacement demand in emerging markets.
West Asia crisis raised logistics costs, freight, insurance and currency volatility; management said freight costs were absorbed in P&L and were the main reason for profit decline.
Mexico Q4 performance was better than Q3, but management did not quantify FY26 Mexico decline.
South Africa emerged as a strong contributor to offset moderation in other markets.
No order pipeline; inventory-led sales model with working capital churn of 2-2.5 times.

qa_highlights.answer: Inventory positioning and customer credit for HexL keep the cash conversion cycle higher; management expects it to ease after the brand is established, next year at the earliest.

qa_highlights.answer: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each; management said Mexico Q4 was stronger than Q3.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is INR300-350 crore; management said each INR100 crore of additional working capital could support roughly INR200-300 crore of revenue after the INR600-700 crore milestone.

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.
544547|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores and consolidated revenue grew 15.9% to INR56.57 crores. Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. Management said inventory of about INR96.8 crores, mostly overseas, is being built as part of the international strategy, and that investments in people and systems will weigh on margins for several quarters.

segments.commentary: Management said it is in early stages, with heavy spending on marketing, discounting and dealer development. Management cited a long-term PAT target of 12% to 14% (also 12% to 15% in an earlier call) and a 20% to 40% retail price advantage versus global brands.

segments.name: New/customised equipment, used and refurbished equipment
segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

Management expects healthier profitability in 2 to 3 years once shipping, interest and manpower costs settle; near-term profit is being sacrificed for long-term build-out.

Post-IPO capital base and enhanced banking facilities cited as capacity to support higher volumes.

Freight and shipping costs rose on geopolitical route closures and longer shipping times, which also lengthened debtor cycles.
Commodity inflation is not expected to be fully passed through; costs are partly absorbed and partly passed to suppliers and customers.
Management said new customised equipment is in highest demand, driven by faster availability and lower breakdown times for end users.
Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects results in 3 to 6 quarters. In 2 to 3 years it targets INR600 crores to INR700 crores revenue with healthier profitability, a dominant international business, and roughly equal revenue from the three verticals.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT fell about 66% YoY, and management is absorbing shipping, interest and manpower costs without a date for recovery.

Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave no segment-level margin or revenue numbers.

Management said the company manufactures backhoe loaders under contract in China, and an analyst raised natural calamities there as a supply risk; management said the locations it uses are unaffected.

544550|2026-03.headline: Pace Digitek Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 60.5% YoY to Rs.1,097 crore; FY26 PAT Rs.307 crore (+10.1%), FY27 revenue guided Rs.3,200-3,400 crore.
544550|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.1,097 crore versus Rs.683 crore a year earlier, driven by project execution. Full-year revenue grew 8.3% to Rs.2,641 crore and PAT rose 10.1% to Rs.307 crore, but full-year EBITDA fell to Rs.455 crore from Rs.482 crore as the mix shifted from telecom to energy. Working capital absorbed cash: inventory was built to Rs.540 crore and trade receivables reached Rs.2,442 crore, which management expects to ease by September 2026. BESS manufacturing capacity is being raised from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026).

544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
544550|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

Peak debt expected at around Rs 1,100 crore of additional borrowing by March 2027, with about Rs 1,600 crore of back-to-back BOT assets.

In-house BESS container facility: trial production from November 2026 and full-scale production from January 2027, expected to meet about 50% of container requirements.
BESS volume target of about 200 containers per quarter; Q2 sold about 91 containers plus 10 in stock (about 100), and Q3 target is slightly below 200.

demand_pricing: Management sees BESS demand of about 30-35 GWh in FY27, rising to about 236 GWh by FY32.

Lithium-ion cell prices rose about 20% in the prior quarter, hurting energy project margins; prices are now falling and expected to stabilise. Tenders bid over the last 3-4 months use the new prices.
Landed Chinese BESS price is roughly in line with Pace's manufacturing cost plus margin.
From January 2027, about 6% export rebate cut on Chinese cell imports; management expects lower cell prices to offset it.

544558|2026-03.headline: Fabtech FY26 total income rose 28.4% to ₹431.33 crore, but margins compressed; management guides ~25% growth and 9.9–10.5% PAT margin.
544558|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income grew 28.4% YoY to ₹431.33 crore and EBITDA rose 18.29% to ₹55.56 crore, while reported net profit fell to ₹38.36 crore from ₹46.45 crore (FY25 included ₹17.85 crore exceptional item). Q4 total income rose 22% YoY to ₹168.24 crore and quarterly net profit rebounded to ₹22.06 crore. Margin pressure was attributed to remobilisation, a 33% rise in RMC cost and a 43% rise in execution cost, amid Middle East disruption. Cash and bank balance rose to ₹208.57 crore after a ~₹230 crore equity infusion (IPO), while receivables rose to ₹204.34 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins shrunk despite revenue growth, and how will investor confidence be regained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project and geography mix (Africa margin pressure), remobilisation, a ~33% RMC cost increase and ~43% execution cost increase; non-contribution margin at 43.8% vs 45.9% last year. Margins expected to improve as internal margin development progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on Q4 and expected impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: No material financial impact per management; freight is the main cost pressure while RMC is sourced in India and revenue is in USD. Delivery delays are possible; no cancellations so far, and clients are discussing variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw-material and freight increases reflected in customer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts contain variation clauses, with post-detailed-engineering items priced at net present value; management says clients accept variations to avoid project delays. It is not a pass-through, but a negotiated outcome that also affects future awards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the ₹900 crore order book by geography and the timeline for conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Split across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kenya, other Africa and North Africa; to be executed over 18–24 months. Billing depends on client readiness to accept materials and complete installation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an active decision: the JBN acquisition in the West is under due diligence and talent acquisition is ongoing. Current borrowings are USD PCFC lines at about SOFR-linked rates plus 200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin target and guidance for FY27 and FY28?

Contribution margin expanded about 910 bps to 46.7%, which management attributes to geography mix (Saudi Arabia, Africa) and project mix, with reduced dependence on UAE. UAE FTS faced war-related headwinds, and several large orders slipped (not cancelled) into later quarters. Management reiterated 20-25% organic growth for FY27, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 stronger, and guided PAT margin of 9-11%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no open credit, with receivables backed by LCs or CAD. Customer advances total about Rs 110 crore, and working cycle is about 120 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UAE weakness cyclical, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UAE demand is focused on high-tech facilities, cell and gene therapy labs and compounding pharmacies, with some projects delayed by geopolitics. It gave no timeline for normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Does the West Asia war affect execution and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said on-site teams kept executing, but conversions slowed as customers delayed decisions. Management said working capital has not been impacted much, and the company is using outsourced labour selectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to percentage-of-completion accounting to smooth quarterly results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is reworking contracts with auditors to define billable milestones tied to percentage completion. Existing contracts stay on shipment/milestone basis, and changes are expected over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: What progress on the IPO-proceeds acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: The Saudi acquisition (SACE, 51%) is complete. The European acquisition is in due diligence and management expects it in the next two to three quarters, with no value disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the margin expansion come from: gross margin or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both: evaluating procurement from China to lift gross margin, and fixed-cost control with operating leverage visible in Q1.

544569|2026-03.headline: Tata Motors Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 24,500 crore with EBITDA margin at 13.9%, but management guided only to single-digit Q1 growth amid commodity and diesel risks.
544569|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter of the year on volume and price, with wholesales of about 131.8K units (up 25% YoY) and standalone EBIT margin of 12.1%. FY26 standalone EBIT crossed 11% for the first time and free cash flow reached about Rs 9,200 crore. Management flagged a sharp commodity cost headwind (about 100 bps in Q4 and significantly higher in Q1 FY27), took only a 2% price increase in April, and said it will not pass through the full cost increase. Iveco deal closure has slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals.

segments.name: Trucks (HCV / ILMCV)
segments.commentary: Management cited highest HCV offtake market share in a decade; ILMCV (5-19 t) showed the highest growth rates through the year. 17 next-gen trucks launched at start of Q4; entire truck range now meets European cabin safety standards.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: Enters FY27 with a solid government order book; 5,000 bus orders secured from STUs during FY26. Management is focused on rebuilding share on a profitable basis; the company is not bidding aggressively on EV bus tenders, calling current quotes unsustainable.

segments.name: SCV Pickup / Small CV
segments.commentary: Ace Pro (launched June 2025) and Intra EV drove volume momentum; EV penetration in SCV pickup rose to about 7% in the last 1-2 months vs about 4% for FY26, with management expecting higher single-digit penetration.

segments.name: Parts & Services / Fleet Edge / Smart City
segments.commentary: Parts and service growth sustained at a higher trajectory; Fleet Edge subscription renewals almost doubled from Q1 to Q4. Smart City has 3,815+ cumulative e-buses deployed, ~59 crore km run, and above 96% uptime.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Largest-ever order of 70,000 Yodha and Ultra T.7 units for Indonesia secured in February; first shipment already at sea after homologation. No shipments to Middle East for the last two months; Sri Lanka under pressure from fuel availability.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 revenue growth guided at single digit, 'if not more', YoY, with management declining to give full-year visibility and pointing to quarter-by-quarter guidance.
Commodity headwind: about 100 bps impact in Q4 FY26, with significantly higher impact expected in Q1 FY27 (steel, aluminium, copper, precious metals, rupee depreciation).
A 2% price increase taken in April 2026; management does not intend to pass through the full commodity increase and will offset through cost levers.
EBITDA margin guidance is 'teens' (corrected from 'mid-teens' on the call), held quarter-by-quarter given cost headwinds.
FY27 investment spend (R&D plus capex) expected broadly in line with FY26 (Rs 3,000 crore); capex guided at 2% to 4% of revenue.

Iveco transaction closure expected in Q2 FY27; financing via bridge loan then refinancing, with the equity/debt mix still open. Final dividend of Rs 4 per share (about Rs 1,500 crore cash outflow) is subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment spend about Rs 3,000 crore: R&D about Rs 1,700 crore and capex plus other investments about Rs 1,100 crore; within the 2%-4% of revenue guidance band.
EV ramp: Intra EV in only its second month of production; management plans to ramp gradually to meet demand.
Electric trucks: 55-ton electric tractor deliveries started with BillionE Mobility; MoU with VOC port (Tamil Nadu) for 40 H2-ICE trucks trials; about 250 electric bus orders received.
Iveco acquisition pending approvals; management said most regulatory approvals are received, with only French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals outstanding.
demand_pricing: Industry TIV grew 19% YoY in Q4 FY26 while Tata Motors volumes grew 25%; FY26 TIV grew 12.5% vs company growth of 11.6%.

Management claims ASPs are rising segment by segment (trucks up YoY); the blended ASP decline is attributed to higher van mix and almost no electric bus sales in FY26.
Diesel is the key monitorable: it is 30-50% of total cost of ownership for transporters; diesel sales rose 8% YoY in March but April was about flat YoY per management.
Heavy-duty customers are postponing purchases toward month-end amid diesel uncertainty; smaller vehicles see lower uncertainty.
E-way bill generation grew 15% YoY in Q4 and 12% YoY in April 2026 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook for MHCV and LCV, and how much risk do fuel price hikes pose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a single-digit Q1 growth 'if not more' and will guide quarter by quarter; diesel prices are the key monitorable as they drive 30-50% of TCO.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost pressure is expected in Q1, how much is being passed on, and what drives margins from here?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps hit in Q4 with a significantly higher impact in Q1; a 2% price increase was taken in April, with the rest absorbed through cost levers to protect demand.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 70,000-unit Indonesia order be executed, and will it finish in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Product is homologated in Indonesia and first shipment is at sea; ramp-up to be rapid, with delivery timeline to be discussed in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is causing the Iveco closure delay, and how does the activist stake affect the deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Most approvals are in; the last two financial regulatory approvals (France and Spain) are pending, pushing closure into Q2 FY27. Management is confident the investor will support the offer.

qa_highlights.question: Are ASPs falling due to discounting or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says segment ASPs are rising; the decline in blended ASP reflects higher van volumes and minimal electric bus sales versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not participating in EV bus tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Quotes in recent CESL tenders are seen as unsustainable; the company was near L2 in one sub-part of the first tender and is pursuing corporate and intercity EV bus demand instead.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 4Q working-capital inflow seasonality still hold, and what is FY27 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 working capital was managed more evenly through the year, with YTD cash flow positive after Q2; FY27 capex guided at 2%-4% of revenue.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, precious metals) and rupee depreciation, with Q1 FY27 impact expected to be significantly higher than Q4's 100 bps.
Diesel prices and their effect on transporter economics and heavy-duty purchase timing; April diesel sales were about flat YoY.
Middle East shipments halted for two months; Sri Lanka fuel shortage; geopolitical disruption to export routes.
Iveco deal: pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals, financing mix (equity vs debt) still undecided, and an activist hedge fund's stake build (6-7%).
Electric bus business: company is holding back from tenders, leaving it out of the EV bus segment for now; EV pickup penetration needs to hold near 7%.
Management has halted its quarterly transporter sentiment survey and is revisiting the methodology.

544569|2026-06.headline: Tata Motors Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 23% to ₹19,300 crore on 26% volume growth; EBITDA margin fell 60 bps to 11.7% on commodity costs.
544569|2026-06.overview: Standalone wholesales reached about 108,700 units, up 26% YoY, with growth in every product line. Revenue grew 23% to ₹19,300 crore and EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at an 11.7% margin, down 60 bps, as steel, aluminium and copper inflation was largely offset by price increases and operating leverage. Free cash flow swung to ₹1,100 crore positive from negative ₹1,800 crore, helped by a ₹3,474 crore working-capital outflow last year that did not recur and by a one-off Indonesia advance. Management guided to a double-digit Q2 domestic growth and a further 2.5% price increase from July 1, while flagging continued commodity pressure.

segments.commentary: 17.1K units, up 16% YoY; VAHAN share dipped slightly on Western Zone supply-chain constraints.

segments.commentary: 18.7K units, up 23% YoY; VAHAN share up about 490 bps; around 4,500 government orders on hand and over 850 e-bus orders.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 domestic CV volumes expected to show healthy double-digit YoY growth, based on July trends.
Further commodity inflation (steel, rubber) expected; net price increase of 2.5% taken from July 1, 2026, with cost management as first line of defence.
Indonesia 70,000-unit order to be supplied over FY27 and FY28; ramp-up under way.
Iveco transaction: final regulatory approval (one pending) expected by end August 2026; tender offer expected early September 2026, closing early November 2026.

Management expects operating leverage to continue as other expenses grow slower than revenue.
capex_capacity: Standalone capex ₹554 crore in Q1, in line with the investment plan.
Intra EV constrained by imported cell supply, not in-house assembly capacity; management expects cell supply debottlenecked by end of Q1 FY27 after orders placed about two months earlier.

Lucknow plant crossed 10 lakh cumulative commercial vehicles produced.
FleetEdge installed base above 1 million vehicles.
demand_pricing: Industry wholesales grew about 18% YoY in Q1; Company volumes grew about 26%. E-way bills up 12.4%, diesel consumption and FASTag collections also rising.
Fleet utilisation improved month on month in Q1 but stayed slightly below Q1 FY26, attributed to high H2 FY26 sales volumes.
Price increases taken during the quarter were largely passed through and added about 140 bps to EBIT margin via realisation (₹402 crore).
Commodity headwind of ₹649 crore (340 bps) on variable costs; volume and mix added ₹686 crore.
Tamil Nadu demand recovering month on month and close to normal in June.
Tipper utilisation seasonally lower during monsoon, expected to pick up mid-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic CV growth be double digit for full year, and how do Indonesia dispatches split across FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early for full-year view; Q2 expected to show double-digit growth. Indonesia 70,000 units to be supplied over FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV demand outlook, Intra EV response and capacity, and will the Q2 price hike cover cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: EV demand seen as positive, with over 850 e-bus orders and further PM e-Bus Sewa tenders expected. Capacity is not the constraint; imported cell lead times are. Further commodity pressure expected; 2.5% net price hike from July 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a limit to price hikes given steel and rubber surges, and how is discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost containment is the first lever; price increases are needed beyond that. The MY26 range helped stabilise prices. Cumulative price increase this year described as significant; no discounting figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital and FCF strength structural or one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly carry-over from Q4 and working-capital discipline plus operating profit. The Indonesia advance was a one-off that helped Q1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: E-truck profitability versus ICE and PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Profitability currently lower than ICE trucks because of low scale; will improve with scale and localisation. Some EV trucks delivered before PLI certificates due to regulatory delays, to meet customer commitments.

qa_highlights.question: How are operators' profitability and freight rates faring after diesel price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no index; anecdotally, diesel increases are being passed through and operator profitability should recover gradually.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, rubber) and further cost pressure in Q2 against a 2.5% July price hike.
Supply constraints in castings, forgings and sheet metal, and imported EV cell lead times, which could cap volumes.
Cash tax now recurring (₹500 crore in Q1 vs ₹20 crore a year earlier); Q1 working-capital benefit partly one-off from Indonesia advance.
Regulatory delay in PLI certificates for EV trucks, with some vehicles delivered before PLI approval.
Iveco transaction approval timing (one approval pending) and tender offer schedule.
Fleet utilisation still below prior-year Q1 levels; tipper utilisation seasonality.

544569|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹23,900 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 90 bps to 11.7% as a 590 bps commodity headwind was absorbed.
544569|2026-09.overview: Wholesales grew 42% YoY to 135,100 units, with every segment in double digits and international business up 177% on the Indonesia order. Standalone EBITDA was about ₹2,800 crore (up 31%) and EBIT margin was 9.7%, down 50 bps YoY, as commodity inflation was largely offset by operating leverage, cost efficiency and realisation gains. Free cash flow reached ₹4,600 crore, helped by a ₹2,679 crore working capital release that management said is partly timing-related. Management expects Q3 YoY growth to taper to high single or early double digits, and commodity inflation of a further 150-200 bps in Q3.

Commodity inflation: further increase of around 150-200 bps in Q3 FY27, led by steel and rubber. YoY commodity impact is about 540 bps; QoQ (Q1 to Q2) was 200 bps.
Pricing: four actions in FY27 (about 1% in January, 2% in April, 2.5% in July, and 1-2% from 1 October depending on segment). Management said pricing does not fully cover commodity increases.
Working capital: management said part of Q2 working capital release is timing-related and will partly reverse. It expects Q3 and Q4 FCF to remain positive, with Q4 seasonally strong.

IVECO: open offer acceptance period runs to 26 October 2026, offer price raised to EUR14.40 (best and final). About 35% of shares tendered as of 22 October. Settlement expected 30 October 2026, subject to conditions. IVECO consolidation begins next quarter (Q3).
EV salience in SCV pickups expected to rise above Q2's ~12% in Q3 and Q4, with management seeing a potential of up to 20%. Driver is Delhi-NCR EV-only registration rule from 1 January.

Capacity constraints are in the supply chain (castings, machining, sheet metal stamping, proprietary items and imported EV aggregates, especially battery cells). Some demand was lost in ILMCV and electric SCV.
Targeted in-house debottlenecking was done in Q2 and will continue through Q3 and partly in Q4, in anticipation of Q4 demand. No new large capacity addition was announced.
Smart City e-bus operations maintain more than 95% fleet uptime and have covered over 64 crore green km since inception.
demand_pricing: Industry CV offtake grew 28.4% YoY in Q2 versus Tata Motors' 30.5%. Fleet utilisation improved gradually through Q2 and freight rates strengthened, though transporter profitability was hit early in the quarter by the diesel price increase.

Domestic ASPs rose QoQ and YoY, but total ASP was flat because of the higher mix of light and small commercial vehicles in the Indonesia export order. International business remains margin accretive, though Indonesia is ASP-dilutive.
Commodity headwind of 590 bps in Q2 EBIT margin walk; steel at a 52-week high, up about 40% YoY. Management has requested a review of the steel safeguard duty through SIAM and other channels.
Interest rates: a 25 bps hike has been taken. Management flagged diesel prices and interest rates as key demand monitorables.
No credit stress seen among transport financiers the company has spoken to. Management says they are in a good place, though not all financiers were engaged.
Non-cyclical business is about 20% of revenue, a stated focus area to offset cyclicality.

qa_highlights.question: How much more commodity pressure is expected next quarter, and what price hikes have been taken?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indonesia delivery plan for FY27-FY28, and is there repeat business beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The ~70,000-unit order will be delivered over FY27 and FY28, currently at 4,500-5,000 units per month. Management is building retail finance, distribution and service in Indonesia and plans to use the opening to sell other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hurdle to reaching the 80% IVECO threshold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the transaction is progressing in line with expectations. It cited the IVECO EGM approval and the best-and-final EUR14.40 offer, and expects tendering to be concentrated in the final 24-48 hours.

qa_highlights.question: Is there concern on transporter sentiment given lower YoY utilisation in HCV, ICV cargo and SCV?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation started weaker in Q2 but improved consistently through the quarter, which gave management enough confidence that it is in a good place.

qa_highlights.question: Are export margins accretive and why were ASPs flat?
qa_highlights.answer: International is margin accretive, but Indonesia is LCV-and-below and so ASP-dilutive. Domestic ASPs rose QoQ and YoY; the flat total ASP reflects the mix shift to smaller vehicles in the Indonesia order.

segments.name: Digital

guidance_outlook: Desk count expected at about 150,000-155,000 by March 2027 (145,300 at Sept 30; ~4,500 added by Oct 5, so already ~150,000); some March deliveries could slip to early April.
Longer term: path to about 190,000-200,000 seats, with FY28 and FY29 supply under negotiation; management says FY28 rollout will be higher than FY27.
Margins: Q3 and Q4 to see further expansion as occupancy rises, with larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire; capacity additions lower in the next two quarters.
FY27 capex about INR500-odd crore for the full year (H2 lower than H1's INR363.8 crore, though one large deal adds capex). FY28 capex likely near INR600 crore or slightly more.
FCFO-to-EBITDA conversion expected in a 1.2x-1.5x range.
PAT margin hovering in 7%-10% range going forward; EBITDA margin range of 20%-23% for next year, depending on capacity timing.
Largest-ever deal to be announced next quarter; expected to require significant capex on a single asset.
capex_capacity: Desks at 145,300 across 85 centres in 8 cities (+27% YoY); ~11,700 desks added in Q2 (record), ~18,400 in H1, ~4,500 more in October.
Bengaluru 54,000 desks (anchor); Hyderabad 20,000 (now second-largest, overtook Mumbai); Pune 17,000.
Q2 additions: Chennai ~3,600 desks (managed office extension), Hyderabad ~2,700 (WeWork-branded), Pune ~2,600 (managed offices).

Pipeline: 9,000+ desks under signed leases and fit-out, ~38,000 seats under LOI; total ~47,000 incremental seats (32% above current capacity). Management cites a further ~2 million sq ft of prospective space not yet at LOI stage.
Growth centres (open <12 months) hold ~25,000 desks; portfolio breakeven occupancy 55.7%. Refurbishment cycles expected around year 5-7 per asset.
demand_pricing: Revenue-to-rent multiple at an all-time high of 2.7x; new large managed-office deals are at about 3x, driven by higher capex per sq ft.
Contracted escalations of 6%-7% on existing contracts; renewal rate about 80%-85% in H1 FY27; churn lower than expected.
Average commitment term rose to about 28 months (larger accounts ~32 months).
Locked-in core revenue grew ~66% to INR3,843 crore against INR1,421 crore of rent, about 2.7x coverage (management also cites ~2.9x in Q&A).
Enterprises 77% of core revenue; GCCs ~41% of mix; other global companies ~26%; Fortune 500 ~30%; top 10 members 23% of revenue.
Minimum wage increases in Karnataka near 60% and backdated BESCOM energy tariffs pressured opex per sq ft in H1; management says margin would be ~22%-23% without these.

qa_highlights.question: How has underwriting changed for new centres (payback, revenue-to-rent) given rising competition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is taking larger positions in Grade A assets, underwriting buildings under development, and doing multi-property deals; it says underwriting is smarter but not drastically changed versus two years ago. Payback periods are improving and capex control is driving better returns.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal trends and pricing on renewals versus new contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal rate 80%-85% in H1; renewal escalations are lower than contracted escalations and pricing on fill-up, as management trades price for loyalty and scale. Around 50% of customer growth comes from existing members expanding.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation between expansion and FCF, and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: More FY28 expansion is planned with additional capex; the company is also looking at buybacks or dividends once book losses are cleared, and at investing in adjacent businesses that help Indian companies scale.

qa_highlights.question: Customization revenue in Q2 and EBITDA flow-through; GCC hiring outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization was about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA; management says large lumpiness is normalised. Management sees GCCs continuing to set up in India and expects demand to grow, with premium managed offices and more amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Will March 2027 desk target of 155,000 be met, and what H2 margin uplift to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Already at about 150,000 desks; 155,000 visibility by March, though some deliveries may slip into early April. Margins to expand further in Q3 and Q4, with the larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire. Q4 YoY margin change expected to be modest given a strong Q4 last year.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for next year and pipeline beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise percentage guidance; FY28 EBITDA margin range of 20%-23%, depending on capacity timing. Pipeline: about 2 million sq ft of additional prospective space not yet signed; leases signed about 12 months out with ~95% visibility, 70%-80% at 18-24 months.

risks_watch: Opex inflation: Karnataka minimum wage hikes near 60% and BESCOM backdated energy tariffs; margin outlook depends on it.
Depreciation rising with the largest capex cycle; PAT margin guided at 7%-10%.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (~1.2 million sq ft built-to-suit campus in Manyata, a customer for ~7 years) is expected to move out; timing uncertain. Another possible lumpy move-out next year.
Promoter pledge still outstanding; management says it will reduce it over time, with no block sale at current prices, and has three years to repay the debt.
Capex upside risk if more managed-office deals are signed; one very large deal to be announced next quarter.
Desk target of 155,000 by March 2027 could slip into early April.

544572|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
544572|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

guidance_outlook: Margin (excl. one-offs) expected to return to around 13% by end of calendar 2026 as demerger costs finish and distribution mix recovers.

New Pune plant expected to start operating mid-2028, with full channel transfer and ramp-up complete by end of calendar 2028.
Tapered roller bearing capacity at Pune raised from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces via machine upgrades; cost down about 18%, changeover time down 20%, new product lead time down about 35%.
Until the new plant is ready, SKF India Limited continues job-work manufacturing; additional demand sourced from SKF Ahmedabad and Nilai.

Q4 margin was pressured by OEM mix (lower margin) and higher employee cost from full 100% bonus accrual versus partial payout in Q3.

Other expenses rose on royalty and trademark payments (about INR 60 million higher) and manufacturing costs (repairs, power and fuel, stores). A transfer pricing margin on services from SKF India was also booked.
Competition described as intense, especially at OEMs. Rupee depreciation is a bigger cost headwind than steel and oil-linked inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 segment-wise mix across general machinery, heavy industries, metals, railway, wind, OEM, aftermarket and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags are extra investments in Pune including the new plant, intense OEM competition, higher railway mix, and higher depreciation. Management targets around 15% through 2030 and says 16-18% is an aspiration that cannot yet be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30. New Pune plant expected to be operational mid-2028, with full ramp-up and channel transfers complete by end of 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 350-400 crore channel expansion investment and how will growth be delivered until the new plant is ready?
qa_highlights.answer: The investment is plant and machinery for DGBB and TRB channels at the new Pune plant, not warehouses. Growth is guided at about 8% in the interim, supported by job-work from SKF India and sourcing from Ahmedabad and Nilai.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the demerger cost roll-off, distribution mix recovery, and price pass-through of FX and 3-4% cost escalation, especially with OEM customers.
Rupee depreciation and steel and oil-linked costs could widen the cost gap.

544572|2026-06.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.
544572|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 9,708 million, up 18.3% YoY (on management's constructed comparison) and 2.6% QoQ. PBT was INR 869 million, a margin of about 9%, hit by roughly INR 147 million of forex loss and about INR 150 million of demerger-related IT separation cost. Operating cash conversion was 63%, with a one-time outflow for name change and land transfer. Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

guidance_outlook: Long-term PBT margin guidance of 14-16%, described as conservative; aspiration 17-19%, with near-term pressure from investments through 2028.
Management expects demerger IT costs to continue for two more quarters, tapering by end-2026 and ceasing around Q4/Q1 FY28.
Management said ~12% is a fair margin on current performance excluding the one-offs; manufacturing efficiency could add a couple of percentage points more.
Aspiration to double the India Industrial business in about five years, with no firm timeline committed.

capex_capacity: New Pune factory is the key constraint: majority of new channel installations are tied to the factory coming online in 2028; capacity is currently constrained by space, not demand.
New tapered roller bearing (TRB) line in Pune adds 3 million units annually, serving agriculture, gearbox and aftermarket; supports exports too.
One additional TRB channel to be added by early 2027 despite capacity constraints.
Plan to add around 15-20 lines, some transferred from SKF group companies and some new; most depend on the new factory.
Capex plan quoted as INR 900-950 crore in prepared remarks and INR 850-900 crore in later Q&A; figures are inconsistent in the transcript.
demand_pricing: Order book reported as growing, with sustained growth over the last few quarters.
INR 140 crore gearbox-manufacturer order (wind-related, one-year, spread through the year) and INR 35 crore agricultural tractor OEM contract.
Innovation traction strongest in general machinery (gearboxes, motors, pumps); agriculture uses customised offerings.
Data center and humanoid opportunities are early-stage; current data center traction is in basic pumps, with no material revenue yet.
Management said the Indian Automotive sales share is being reduced to improve mix.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin moderation from the 16-19% guidance to 14-16%, and how much is FX and demerger impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14-16% is the conservative long-term path and 17-19% the aspiration; near-term margins dip due to investments. CFO quantified FX plus demerger one-offs at about 3% of margin, implying ~12% underlying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply and recurrence profile of the INR 140 crore wind and INR 35 crore agri orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are one-time or one-year contracts, typically extending one to two years. Some services and condition-monitoring contracts are longer-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference across distribution, OE and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Solutions are around 6-7% of India business, below 10% in aspiration. Doubling the business is an aspiration within five years at the outside, with no committed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will one-off costs end, and is 12% margin achievable now?
qa_highlights.answer: The IT cost should taper through end-2026 and stop around Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28. CFO said ~12% is a fair current margin, with further gains from efficiency and the Pune plant.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company merge with the SKF automotive or other group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no active plans; it wants the demerger to stabilise first but continuously evaluates options.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation linked to Middle East tensions raised import costs on European-sourced products; margin impact depends on INR movement.

Capacity constraint until the 2028 Pune plant; growth above current capacity is limited, with only one added TRB channel by early 2027.

544574|2026-09.headline: Tata Capital Q2 FY27 consolidated AUM rose 26% YoY to INR3,08,030 crore and PAT grew 51% YoY to INR1,660 crore.
544574|2026-09.overview: Consolidated AUM crossed INR3 lakh crore, growing 26% YoY and 6% QoQ, with 32% YoY growth excluding Motor Finance. PAT rose 51% YoY to INR1,660 crore, ROA was 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance) and ROE exceeded 14%. Credit cost eased to 0.9% from 1.0% in Q1 and Stage 3 was stable at 1.9%, while NIM plus fee fell about 10 bps QoQ. Management guided to a 25 bps repo hike in October and a 20-25 bps PLR increase effective 1 November, and said it expects no further NIM plus fee drag in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4. Revolving credit and insurance commission regulations remain open risks, with no quantification given.

segments.name: Tata Capital Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR95,098 crore (+26% YoY, +6% QoQ), PAT INR552 crore, ROA 2.5%, ROE 18%. Affordable and micro housing AUM grew 22% YoY and 5% QoQ; 23 new locations added in the quarter.

segments.name: Retail and SME
segments.commentary: Retail and SME make up 85.4% of consolidated AUM. Supply chain has diversified, with auto now about 35% of supply chain versus about two-thirds four years ago.

segments.name: High-margin businesses
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 40% YoY while AUM growth rose to 14% from 10% in Q1; management expects AUM growth to reach overall portfolio levels by Q4.

segments.name: Motor Finance (TMFL)
segments.commentary: Portfolio is still running down, with the Q2 rundown below Q1 and Q1 below Q4 FY26. Management expects stabilisation in Q3 and growth from Q4. Share of the book fell from 14.5% in March 2025 to about 7.7%. Gross NPA rise is attributed to seasonality and a shrinking denominator; absolute Q2 slippages were lower YoY. A macro provision of about INR30 crore was created in CV.

segments.name: Microfinance and flexi loans
segments.commentary: Microfinance is under 1% of the book, with improving asset quality and growth. Retail flexi loans are about 2-2.5% of the book. Management estimates the revolving credit impact at 3-4% of AUM if products cannot be converted.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 23-25% for FY27 and over FY25-FY28; management says it will land within this range and is not looking to revise guidance down.
Management is not revising FY28 ROA and ROE guidance and says it may revise upward at year-end; it is confident of meeting cost-to-income, credit cost and PAT growth guidance.
PLR increase of 25 bps (standalone ALCO) and 20 bps (Housing Finance) effective 1 November 2026, to protect NIM plus fee.
NIM plus fee expected stable in Q3 FY27 and improving distinctly in Q4 FY27.
Management expects about 2 further repo hikes in FY27 (market talk of around 50 bps more).
Income growth expected around 25% and cost growth around 15% for the year.
Capital raise expected in H2 FY28, more towards Q3-Q4, based on the current growth plan.
capex_capacity: Branch network at about 1,515 branches across 1,094 locations in 26 states and UTs; net addition of 24 branches in Q2.
Q3 and Q4 location expansion in affordable and micro housing planned to be stronger than Q2.
Gold loan business is not yet live; launch expected in the coming month.
On-roll employee strength 31,655, with over 80% in frontline sales and collections; headcount up 6% against AUM up 26%.
Over 180 digital partnerships; 9.2 million customers served.
demand_pricing: Management described festive demand as strong across two-wheeler, passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle segments, with dealer supply-chain demand also rising.
Rural growth is slower than urban, but Tata Capital's rural exposure is limited to microfinance; it has no tractor or agri farm loans and hardly any microfinance in Maharashtra.
Housing NIM fell about 5 bps QoQ from competitive pressure in prime home loans; the other 5 bps came from higher cost of funds.
Fee income rose 30% YoY, driven by assignment income (DA income up 58% YoY); non-assignment fee income held at Q1 level as a percentage of AUM.
Management is declining some deals that do not meet margin requirements, prioritising margins over growth.
Floating-rate liabilities are 48% of total liabilities and floating-rate assets 66% of assets.

qa_highlights.question: Path if revolving credit draft norms are adopted, and whether exposure is being cut before final norms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not cut exposure and is piloting alternate products, with more to start in November; it estimates the impact at 3-4% of AUM and believes more than half of flexi can be converted to modified products at similar pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance distribution norms impact and alternative fee sources.
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not quantified the impact, which depends on final regulations. Options include selling retail insurance, growing NIM plus fee, and reducing costs if insurance is not sold.

qa_highlights.question: Motor Finance NPA rise and the timing of book growth.
qa_highlights.answer: The rise reflects seasonality (Q2 typically has the highest NPA growth) and a shrinking denominator; absolute slippages were lower YoY. Portfolio growth is expected to stabilise in Q3 and resume in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: NIM trajectory for H2 FY27 and FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: NIM fell about 10 bps QoQ in Q2 (about 5 bps from cost of funds and 5 bps from prime home loan competition). Management expects stability in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4, and says a rate increase should be neutral to accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the SME growth is channel finance and whether supply-chain growth will shift to retail.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from both term loans and supply chain, with supply chain having a particularly strong quarter. Auto is about 35% of supply chain, down from about two-thirds four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capital raise timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to need capital in H2 FY28, more towards Q3-Q4, and will also consider sub-debt; it did not give a precise size.

qa_highlights.question: Why yields are not rising despite high-margin growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Balance transfer pressure eases in a rising-rate environment, and high-margin AUM growth (14%) is expected to reach overall portfolio growth by Q4. Business-level yield plans are expected to show output from end-Q3 or Q4.

risks_watch: Revolving credit (flexi) and insurance commission regulations could hit fee income and product economics; no quantification given yet.
Repo hikes and tighter liquidity (surplus down below INR1 lakh crore) could push cost of funds higher than the 20-25 bps PLR pass-through.
Motor Finance: Q3 stabilisation and Q4 growth are not yet demonstrated; NPA trend is seasonal.
Drought, fuel prices and CV utilisation could affect the CV book and the rural and microfinance exposure.
Capital: CRAR has fallen about 100 bps per quarter since IPO, with a capital raise expected in H2 FY28.
544574|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and guidance, with explicit reassurance that FY28 targets are unchanged. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on revolving credit and insurance regulation, saying the impact cannot be quantified. Defensive on the Motor Finance growth lag and the Q2 NIM dip.
key_quotes: We do not want growth at the expense of margins.
We expect the portfolio to stabilize in Q3 and start growing from Q4.
We remain on track to deliver our medium-term guidance with operating leverage expected to be an important lever of further improvement in ROA.
Insurance remains an important risk cover for our customers and an integral part of our underwriting framework.

544576|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR80.54 bn (+8.1% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell ~250 bps YoY to 11.7%, with FY27 targeting early double-digit margins.
544576|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was LG Electronics India's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR80.54 bn, up 8.1% YoY, with EBITDA of INR9.45 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of INR6.93 bn (8.5%). Year-on-year margin compression was attributed to channel promotion spend (~1.1 pp), rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY, ~1 pp impact), and e-waste compliance cost (~0.2 pp). For FY26, revenue grew 1.0% to INR246.05 bn, EBITDA was INR24.08 bn (9.8%) and PAT INR16.85 bn (6.8%). Management guided FY27 to mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margins, citing April-May sell-through and recent price hikes.

financial_highlights.change: +8.1% YoY vs INR74.48 bn in Q4 FY25
Margin down ~250 bps YoY; up 7% sequentially

segments.name: Home Appliances & Air Solutions (H&A)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR65.16 bn (+5.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR181.60 bn. EBIT margin 11.9% in Q4, hit by commodity costs, rupee depreciation and channel investments for new launches. Premium washers, French door refrigerators and 5-star RACs saw higher ASPs.

segments.name: Home Entertainment (HE)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR15.37 bn (+19.6% YoY, +15.9% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR64.44 bn. EBIT margin 13.4% in Q4, after time-bound Cricket World Cup marketing spend. OLED market share 60.0% YTD March 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teen percentage; early double-digit EBITDA margin for full year, better than FY26.
Margin recovery levers: localization (55.2% in FY26, targeted +1 to 2 pp per year), operating leverage, richer mix, scaling AMC and B2B, export growth, and industry price increases.
Export expansion targeted 'very significantly' in FY27; large-capacity refrigerators exported to advanced markets from Q1 FY27; Essential Series exports to 22 countries.

Sri City plant: total investment INR50 bn, funded from internal accruals; compressor line Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), RAC line Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027); washing machine and refrigerator lines to follow in phases.
Management expects ROE and ROCE to improve meaningfully in FY27 as profitability normalizes and Sri City capital starts generating returns.
No immediate plan for further price hikes; monitoring raw material and currency movements.
capex_capacity: Sri City (third factory) total planned investment INR50 bn; about INR6.57 bn deployed to March 2026 (CWIP and capital advances) (INR657 crore per Q&A). Next two years' spend largely planned against the INR5,000 crore total.
Sri City timelines: compressor production Q3 FY27; RAC production Q4 FY27; washing machine and refrigerator lines added thereafter in phases. Hiring for key roles has started.
Pune plant produces premium products: 674 litre and 790 litre side-by-side refrigerators, top freezers (790 litre plus) and front-load washing machines for export.
Sri City expected to double export-capable capacity and improve South India logistics (South India is 38-40% of business).
FY26 capex INR5.51 bn; localization rate 55.2%, up ~1.4 pp YoY.
demand_pricing: Channel: AC channel filled in Q4 (55% of annual AC business falls in Q4); >1 million ACs sold in Q4 FY26; industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, but March cold spell slowed sell-out. LG says its inventory was in line with plan and manageable.

Price hikes: RAC increased in two phases (BEE-rating driven, then input cost and FX), about 12-13% per analyst; refrigerators and washing machines also repriced. LG says competitive positioning unchanged and no impact on sales.

New categories: French door refrigerator share rose from 5% to 14% by March 2026 after December 2025 launch; chest freezer (market ~INR3,000 crore, five models coming); fixed-speed RAC entry; dishwashers doubled revenue in FY26 and rank #2.
Essential Series (launched 14 Oct 2025): about 100,000 washing machines sold in Q4 FY26; ~80,000 Essential refrigerators in Q4; ~20,000 sub-1-ton RACs (0.8 ton).
TV: 55-inch and above segment grew 47% and now 49% of business; TV revenue grew 20%+ in Q4.
AC penetration in India cited at ~13%; B2B order inflows from government, corporate and hospitality; ID division hit record quarterly sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth of 8% not translate into operating leverage and a YoY margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said margin fell ~250 bps: channel promotion ~1.1 pp (temporary, to drive sell-out and partner confidence), currency depreciation ~1 pp, and e-waste compliance ~0.2 pp as recycling target rose from 60% to 70%. Price hikes, lower promotions and summer demand are expected to restore margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is LG doing differently from peers, and how will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Dongmyung Seo cited export scaling, the recovering B2B business, AMC as a high-margin recurring stream, and new categories. Margin levers: exports (core growth engine), localization (55.2%), and a higher mix of AMC and B2B. Lower oil prices after Middle East stabilisation could also help.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel inventory now versus the start of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinder Singh said the AC industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, with dealers cautious after a slow March. LG's inventory was aligned with plan, and current high temperatures are easing channel pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are price hikes enough to protect margins, and are more planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said AC prices were raised in two calibrated phases and that LG was first to move, with competitors following. Similar hikes were made on refrigerators and washers with no volume impact. No immediate further hikes are planned, but the company is monitoring raw materials and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for FY27 and the Sri City timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna confirmed the Sri City plant is on track: compressor line in Q3 FY27, RAC line in Q4 FY27, and washing machine and refrigerator lines later. About INR657 crore is spent to March 2026, with the full INR5,000 crore to be funded from internal accruals over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Does LG still target doubling exports, and what is the Essential Series response?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna reiterated a very significant export expansion, with premium products to developed markets from Pune and Sri City. Sanjay Chitkara said Essential Series sales were encouraging, with 100,000 washers and 80,000 refrigerators in Q4, and exports are going to 22 countries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for April-May 2026 and the industry growth comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said ACs are well supported by summer demand and the company expects good growth. He targets strong double-digit to mid-teen growth across all four categories in FY27, but gave no industry growth figures for April-May.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the new categories are for domestic or export use?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said the new categories serve both: chest freezers (five models, market ~INR3,000 crore), fixed-speed RACs, and large refrigerators from Pune, which target new domestic business and global markets.

risks_watch: Rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY in Q4) and commodity costs, with management noting currency and geopolitical (US-Iran, Middle East) risks to FY27 costs.
Whether promotional intensity falls and price hikes stick, which underpin the early double-digit EBITDA margin target.

Return ratios (ROE, ROCE) moderated in FY26 due to high cash balance and H1 headwinds; improvement depends on Sri City returns.

544576|2026-06.headline: LG Electronics India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.5% to INR72.33 billion and EBITDA margin expanded 110 bps to 12.5%.
544576|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 15.5% YoY to INR72.33 billion, with every key category growing double digits on both volume and value. EBITDA rose 26.2% to INR9.04 billion, with margin up 110 bps YoY to 12.5% on product mix, calibrated price increases and operating leverage. PAT grew 27.2% to INR6.53 billion (8.9% margin). Management highlighted record quarterly exports to over 60 countries, Sri City capex of INR5.88 billion out of INR7.36 billion total, and a fully internally funded plan with no external borrowing.

financial_highlights.change: +110 bps YoY (11.4%); +0.8 pp QoQ per IRO
INR5.88 billion deployed at Sri City

segments.name: Home Appliance and Air Solution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55.77 billion, up 13.6% YoY; segment EBIT up about 13.8% to about INR6.4 billion, margin steady at 11.5%. Premium French door refrigerators, 8 kg+ washing machines and dishwashers grew well ahead of portfolio.

segments.name: Home Entertainment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR16.57 billion, up 22.3% YoY; segment EBIT up 48.5% YoY with margin expanding to 19%. TV revenue grew about 25%; 55-inch and above grew about 53% and now contributes about 50% of TV business.

segments.name: Information Display (within Home Entertainment)
segments.commentary: Management cited LED signage at its highest ever quarterly sales and a 36% market share, about 5 pp ahead of the number 2 player. Growth came from government and corporate orders.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 demand to be broad-based, with TV and washing machines expected to drive H2 growth; AC and refrigerators to benefit from premiumisation and replacement.
Q2 channel stocking underway ahead of Onam, Durga Puja and Diwali; launch pipeline described as full.
Exports: management says it will hit its yearly export target but gave no numeric guidance; export margins are described as better than domestic.
Sri City capitalisation expected to begin in H2 FY27; initial incremental costs expected near term.
Localisation target of 65% over the next 3 to 4 years, from 55.2% in the last full year.
Dividend to be reviewed as Sri City progresses and cash generation strengthens; current year dividend decision was made with capex priorities in mind.
Commercial AC business: management is confident of a 20% CAGR trajectory, as achieved over FY22 to FY25.

Sri City adds 2 million AC capacity; Greater Noida has 1 million AC capacity and 7 million refrigerator capacity.
Investment expected to almost double manufacturing capacity and position India as an export hub; funded entirely by internal accruals with no external debt.
Pune and Greater Noida plants being expanded for new Essential family sizes and premium products.
Data-centre cooling: mid-scale projects already live using Multi V VRF and chiller systems; hyperscale is at a preliminary stage, with partnerships under evaluation.
demand_pricing: Calibrated price increases were taken in selected categories and absorbed well; further pricing will depend on input costs.
Essential Series sold over 500,000 units in January to June 2026, exceeding plan; margins in line with the B2C portfolio, not dilutive; exported to 22 countries.
Exports grew 30% in Q1; LG now supplies over 60 countries (65 per Co-CSMO) versus 45 to 47 at the time of IPO.

Government notified quantitative restrictions on compressor imports from 8 May: reciprocating compressors restricted up to 60% and rotary compressors up to 70% (per management, against FY25 levels). Management sees this as positive for cost and share.
