qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra (J.P. Morgan): How sustainable is Home Entertainment growth, and how much is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said TV grew about 25% for a second straight quarter, with growth from both volume and value; 55-inch and above grew about 53% and now is about 50% of TV business. He called the growth structural and not seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra: Export growth, US and Europe contribution, FY27 export target, and export margins versus domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew 30% in Q1. Two pillars: premium products to key global markets and Essential Series to Asia, Middle East and Africa. Export margins are better than domestic. No numeric FY27 target was given beyond saying the yearly target will be hit.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavani K (Axis): Key growth drivers for FY27 and long-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Soonjoo Seo cited exports scaling, premiumisation across categories (large TVs, French door and side-by-side refrigerators, 8 kg+ washing machines, 5-star inverter ACs), and India's role in the global south strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavani K: What is the impact of the revised compressor import policy, given the Q3 compressor facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaganjeet Singh said the policy is positive: LG has 1 million AC capacity at Greater Noida plus 2 million at Sri City, and 7 million refrigerator capacity at Greater Noida, which is above internal needs. Management expects a cost advantage and share gains in refrigerators and ACs.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama): B2B performance and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said B2B grew strongly; LED signage had its highest ever quarterly sales; commercial AC is expanding distribution and 2-ton 4-star models. Management is confident of a 20% CAGR, as delivered over FY22 to FY25. No Q1 B2B revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: How is raw material cost inflation being managed, and what is the Q2 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaganjeet Singh listed localisation (including a resin localised in Q1), flexible local and import sourcing, multiple suppliers, and value engineering. Calibrated price increases are already taken; further action depends on input costs. No Q2 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Siddharth Bora (Nomura): Category-wise FY27 growth outlook, and is Q1 representative?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said all products grew double digits in Q1 and demand is healthy across segments. TV and washing machines are expected to drive H2 growth. No category growth numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Siddharth Bora: Essential Series volume, revenue contribution, further SKUs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinderjeet Singh said over 500,000 units were sold in six months, margins are in line with the B2C portfolio, refrigerator range expanded to 225, 251 and 276 litres, and a higher-capacity top loader is planned. No revenue share was given.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Goel (HSBC): Localisation path from 55% and bottlenecks to 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said localisation was 55.2% in the last full year, improving 2-3 pp a year, with a target of 65% over the next 3 to 4 years. Sri City AC compressors and local side-by-side refrigerator production at Pune are key steps.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Goel: Data-centre cooling readiness and dividend or capital return plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mid-scale data-centre cooling is already live with Multi V and chillers; hyperscale is preliminary, with partner-led routes under evaluation and not a key FY27 driver. 544595|2026-09.headline: Orkla India Q2 FY27 revenue grew 18.4% to INR776 crore (19.4% on revenue from operations) with volume up 2.9%; EBITDA margin 15.9%, down ~100 bps YoY.

EBITDA rose 12.6% to INR124 crore, but margin moderated about 100 bps YoY as pricing lagged input costs and Project Bolt and PLI effects weighed. Management said underlying EBITDA growth was 11.6% excluding PLI and Project Bolt investments, and H1 underlying margin was 17.2%. Kerala distribution restructuring and Project Bolt (quick commerce) are showing early results, with digital commerce rising to 10% of domestic revenue.

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Revenue +25.1% YoY, largely price-led (pricing ~20%+), with positive volume but moderated by inflation and Kerala restructuring. Chilli and coriander drove the inflation. Spices grew about 48% YoY in value per the appendix, per management.

segments.name: Convenience foods
segments.commentary: Revenue +7.7% YoY against a high base because festive season shifted into Q3 (Dussehra and Diwali). Sequential growth continued; volume growth moderated.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue +20% YoY, with Eastern leading growth; volumes grew despite price inflation and festive timing shift.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.7% YoY; GCC +22.7% YoY, described as the key growth engine.

segments.name: Digital commerce
segments.commentary: Share of domestic business rose from 8.9% in Q1 FY27 to 10% in Q2 FY27; rest-of-India digital commerce revenue +33.6% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to grow well beyond 10-12% revenue growth; if commodity inflation moderates to 5-7%, it sees potential for 8-10% volume growth.
Pricing actions taken late in Q2 are expected to flow through with full benefit in Q3, which should aid margins.
Standalone modern trade restructuring about 50% complete; remainder to finish by December 2026.
Kerala spices distribution rollout to continue through March 2027, starting with Kasaragod and Kannur.
Project Bolt is entering its final quarter of implementation; festive sweets and meals platforms to be tested through Q3.
capex_capacity: Kerala convenience foods distribution separation completed in June 2026; effective coverage up about 10% (1.1x) and sales productivity up 1.27x vs Q4 FY26 levels.
Wet batter (MTR Minute Fresh) launched in Hyderabad about 3 months ago, with 5-7% market share; Bangalore was the only prior market. Next large cities to follow after Hyderabad stabilises.
Project Bolt present in about 240 towns across rest of India; focus on top 28 cities; consumer reach has tripled through social content.
Around 15 new sweets launches for the festive season via digital commerce; 38 launches in H1 (23 in Q1, 15 in Q2).
Management did not disclose capex amounts or capacity figures in the call.
demand_pricing: Spice price increases of over 20% taken to pass through commodity inflation; pure spices priced at roughly 10% over raw commodity wholesale price; blended spices on a more calibrated approach.
Spice volumes slightly moderated due to price elasticity; company does not disclose volume by category or geography.
Spice prices stabilised after crop cycle ended and stock moved to cold storage; a speculative spike in late September triggered another price increase.
Organised share of South Indian spice market about 40% (up from 30-35% over five years), with 60% unorganised.
Quick commerce: dry batter has very little competition (dominant); wet batter No. 2 brand; sweets segment highly competitive (Haldiram and others); meals segment fragmented.
Digital commerce mix is margin accretive at gross margin level because of higher convenience food share.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth detail for spices and convenience foods?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give category volume numbers; both categories had positive volume, with spices volume moderated by 20%+ pricing and convenience foods moderated by the festive shift into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Price breakdown for blended vs pure spices, drivers of the 48% spice increase, and current price trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Pure spices track commodity moves directly; blended spices priced more calibrated. Chilli and coriander drove the inflation. Prices now largely stable after crop cycle ended, with one speculative spike in late September.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala distribution restructuring status, volume and share impact, and H2 milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Convenience food separation completed June 2026; standalone modern trade about 50% done, to finish by December 2026; spice coverage expansion just started in Kasaragod and Kannur. Standalone modern trade volume +16% QoQ; Kerala spice volume returned positive in Q2 due to Onam.

qa_highlights.question: Wet batter scaling and Project Bolt competition in rest of India?
qa_highlights.answer: Wet batter now in Hyderabad (3 months) with 5-7% share, to stabilise before next large cities. Project Bolt covers about 240 towns; quick commerce is the main lever; competition differs by segment.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term volume vs price contribution and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to grow beyond 10-12%; if inflation moderates to 5-7%, possible 8-10% volume growth. Believes category can take 2-3% price increases given spices are only 2.5-3% of consumer spend.

qa_highlights.question: Margin glide path, especially at Eastern, and impact of restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Eastern mix is about 50% pure spices, 45% blended spices and the balance convenience foods; plan is to build convenience foods to lift margins, alongside consolidated manufacturing and digitisation efficiency programmes. No numeric margin target given.

Volume elasticity from 20%+ spice price increases; volume growth only 2.9% in Q2.

Kerala restructuring and Project Bolt investments weighing on EBITDA growth (ex-PLI and Bolt, growth 11.6%).
Competitive intensity in sweets and meals segments in quick commerce; wet batter No. 2 position.
Reliance on PLI benefits in PAT; other income from surplus cash supporting profit.

544597|2026-03.headline: Piramal Finance FY26 consol net profit rose to INR1,506 crore (3x YoY); Q4 Growth RoAUM 2.1%, with FY27 exit guidance of 2.5%.
544597|2026-03.overview: Consolidated AUM grew 25% YoY to about INR1,01,230 crore, with Growth AUM up 33% to INR98,423 crore and the Legacy book cut 59% to INR2,807 crore. Q4 Growth PBT was INR495 crore (up 61% YoY) and consolidated net profit was INR502 crore versus INR102 crore a year earlier. Management attributed the step-up in profit partly to one-time gains from the Piramal Imaging deferred consideration and the Shriram Life stake sale, part of which was used to take markdowns and build buffers. Domestic ratings moved to AA+ across all three agencies, and FY27 guidance is ~25% AUM growth, ~50% consol profit growth and ~2.5% exit RoAUM.

segments.name: Retail (Growth)
segments.commentary: Retail AUM INR85,885 crore (85% of total), up 33% YoY; Q4 disbursements INR13,101 crore (+34% YoY). Retail 90+ DPD 0.6%, down 20 bps QoQ; retail opex/AUM 3.6%, down 21 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Mortgages (HL + LAP)
segments.commentary: Mortgage AUM INR57,837 crore, up 32% YoY; 57% of total AUM and 67% of retail AUM. Smaller-ticket MSME mortgages, previously flagged, stabilised in Q4.

segments.name: Wholesale 2.0
segments.commentary: AUM INR12,538 crore, up 38% YoY; real estate:CMML mix 73:27, average ticket INR53 crore, yield 14.4%, zero NPAs. FY26 disbursements INR9,292 crore; repayments INR5,859 crore (about 63% of disbursements).

segments.name: Legacy
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,807 crore, down 59% YoY and under 3% of total AUM (66% four years ago). Management expects it to become immaterial by Q4 FY27 and to stop separate reporting during FY27.

segments.name: Gold and rural (new)
segments.commentary: Gold loans: 22 branches launched in Maharashtra and Telangana (13 disbursement-active), target about 200 branches in FY27. Rural: 136 branches; micro loans AUM INR1,384 crore, up 42% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27: total AUM growth of about 25% YoY.
FY27: consolidated profit growth of about 50%.
Exit FY27 at about 2.5% RoAUM (vs 2.1% in Q4 FY26); management says this holds even with some credit cost normalisation.
Rating upgrade to AA+ could cut cost of borrowing by 50-80 bps as the liability stack churns over about three years; steady-state ROE could rise 3-4 percentage points.
Retail opex/AUM expected to fall a little further in FY27; management cites about 50 bps more room. Unsecured mix to rise 400-500 bps.
Tax: about INR16,000 crore of future profit is shielded by accumulated losses (about INR24,500 crore gross); effective tax rate can be modelled very low until about 2032.
capex_capacity: Branch network 701 at March 2026 (crossed 700 in Q4); Q4 added 26 urban full-service, 22 gold and 60 rural branches; management target about 880 branches per the presentation.
Gold loans: plan to add about 180 branches in FY27 to reach about 200; a gold branch costs about one-third of an urban branch's annual opex.
Rural branches cost about one-tenth of an urban branch to set up.
Capital: CRAR 19.8%; management would consider raising capital at 17.5-18%. Net capital consumption in Q4 was only 50 bps, giving roughly 3-4 quarters of runway.
Net worth to net owned funds gap (INR2,500-2,700 crore each from BAU deductions, DTA of INR2,700 crore, and investments) should narrow by about one-third as investments are divested.
demand_pricing: Wholesale repayments are strong: Q4 repayments were about 82% of Q4 disbursements, and about 50% of FY27 contractual repayments are already received.
Digital unsecured loans are performing well, but management will cut them quickly if risk curves turn (it cut digital by over 60% in FY25).
Cross-sell is about 30% of unsecured disbursements, expected to rise materially.
Watch list expanded beyond F&B MSMEs to travel and logistics, textiles, gems and jewellery, and food processing. Bounce rates in April matched March; no visible retail risk impact yet.
Management expects any Middle East war effect on unsecured 90+ DPD to show around July-August (Q2), not in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What drives Growth NIM beyond 7%, and does consol NIM converge with it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects consol and Growth NIM to converge in the latter half of FY27. Levers are asset mix (unsecured +400-500 bps, gold) and cost of borrowing, with AA+ benefit of 50-80 bps over about three years.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 fee income looked low as a share of retail AUM; where should it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was depressed by a one-time reversal of fee income to help its 50%-owned life insurance associate. Fee income should return to normal, and the 70-90 bps level was seen as reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 2.5% exit RoAUM hold if credit cost rises toward 1.9-2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said opex/AUM (about 50 bps more to go) and cost of borrowing gains should absorb the credit cost normalisation. Mix is shifting toward prime-like mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capital and the net worth to NOF gap?
qa_highlights.answer: CRAR is 19.8%; the gap between net worth and NOF comes from BAU deductions, DTA of about INR2,700 crore and investments. The company has 3-4 quarters of runway before the 17.5-18% raise trigger.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR900 crore fair-value loss and INR590 crore impairment in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described them as pre-emptive markdowns made with the one-time gains (about INR1,300 crore deferred Imaging consideration and about INR250-300 crore Shriram Life gain). About one-third is added buffer; the rest is losses that would have come over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion push up opex/AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Opex/AUM is expected to keep falling in FY27. If the two conflict, management will prioritise the opex curve over branch openings.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: crude and LPG supply, and second-order effects on self-employed and business borrowers, mainly in Q2 FY27.
Q4 credit cost of 1.5% is below the 1.9-2% steady state management cited; any normalisation cuts into the RoAUM path.
Bond market access at AA+ is still untested; no bond issue since the upgrade, and the cost-of-borrowing benefit depends on churn.
Q4 profit included one-time gains and markdowns; sustainability of the consolidated profit growth (about 50%) depends on the Growth book.
Capital: CRAR 19.8% vs 15% requirement; capital raise possible if CRAR falls to 17.5-18%.
Legacy book write-backs of a few hundred crore are expected, but there is no timing.

544597|2026-06.headline: Piramal Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 67% YoY to Rs 461 crore, with Growth AUM up 32% and Growth RoAUM at 1.9%.
544597|2026-06.overview: Total AUM grew 25% YoY to Rs 1,06,940 crore, while Growth business AUM (retail plus wholesale, 98% of total) grew 32%. Growth business PBT was Rs 470 crore versus Rs 294 crore a year ago, and pre-provisioning operating profit rose 89% YoY to Rs 804 crore. Retail disbursements grew 44% YoY, and retail 90+ DPD stayed at 0.7%, though management flagged early-stage stress in IT-sector salaried borrowers and a small LAP uptick. The Board approved an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs 4,000 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 294 crore in Q1 FY26
vs 6.9% in Q1 FY26 and FY26
Growth 1.6% vs 1.5% in Q4 FY26; legacy provisioning raised due to higher stage 2 PCR

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail AUM grew 32% YoY to Rs 91,249 crore; mortgages (HL plus LAP) grew 30% to Rs 61,199 crore, 67% of retail AUM. Unsecured (PL, UBL, digital, rural micro) grew 45% YoY to Rs 21,412 crore, 23% of retail AUM.

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Wholesale AUM grew 27% YoY to Rs 13,238 crore, with a 70:30 real estate to CMML mix and average yield of 14.2%. Disbursed Rs 2,604 crore; repayments were Rs 1,932 crore (74% of disbursements).

segments.name: Legacy
segments.commentary: Legacy AUM fell Rs 355 crore to Rs 2,452 crore, now 2% of total AUM.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated original FY27 guidance on AUM growth, profit growth and RoAUM; Growth RoAUM expected to rise from 1.8-1.9% in Q1 to about 2.5% by Q4 FY27.
Retail OPEX to AUM (3.5% in Q1) expected to fall a further 40-50 bps over the next four to five quarters.
Gold loan branches to rise from 67 to 200 by end-March 2027; PL branch penetration targeted at 100% within two to three quarters.
Leverage target of 4.5-5x AUM to equity is under review; management expects higher leverage as the company moves to AA+.
Enabling resolution for up to Rs 4,000 crore of capital raise, timing and instrument open; no imminent acquisition.
capex_capacity: Branches: net 79 added in Q1 to 780 total; rural branches 178 (from 136); urban full-service branches reduced by eight to 535.
Gold loans network at 67 branches (phase two launched), targeting 200 by March 2027.
Regulatory CRAR 18.85%, with about Rs 9,000 crore gap between net worth and regulatory capital (about Rs 3,000 crore each from BAU deductions, DTAs and investment book); all Tier 1, no Tier 2.
Average quarterly capital consumption about 63 bps last year; DTA utilisation and investment sell-downs expected to release capital but not within the next two to three quarters.
demand_pricing: Retail disbursements grew 44% YoY in Q1 versus 34% in Q4 FY26 and 31% in FY26.
Wholesale: prepayments high; about 61% of FY27 contractual repayments already received; management attributes this mainly to operating cash flows running ahead of underwriting in real estate.

Mortgage competition: management says the number of players is unchanged; small-ticket housing (under Rs 35 lakh) industry growth is low single digit, and the company operates at about 12.5% yield in that segment.
Yield on loans stable at 13.2-13.4%; retail total income to loans down 26 bps YoY to 14.7% after fewer direct assignment (DA) sell-downs.
Partnerships/digital volumes rising with Fintech activity; more than 80% under FLDG; management will cut volumes if risk rises.

qa_highlights.question: Is salaried stress broader, given the strong salaried PL push? How is digital (embedded) scaling after an earlier slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Discomfort is limited to IT-sector salaried customers, mainly in South India; IT is about 13% of the unsecured salaried base. Early bounce rates are rising in secured products; unsecured is behaving well. Digital volumes are high because risk is at historically low levels and can be cut quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated cost of funds be passed on to floating-rate mortgage customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds has not risen yet and was down; prime lending rate was not cut through the down cycle. Floating-rate customers will see rate moves in both directions, with lower amplitude.

qa_highlights.question: What drives RoAUM from 1.8-1.9% to 2.5% by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is the seasonal low because annual people-cost increments hit in Q1; a larger book originated through the year and flat staff cost should lift RoAUM by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why are wholesale prepayments so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly operating cash flows ahead of underwriting in real estate; in CMML, refinancing by banks, capital-market raises and cash flows are all contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is disbursement yield above portfolio yield, and why has portfolio yield not risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-duration, higher-yield products are over-represented in disbursements, so AUM yield runs below disbursement yield structurally. Direction holds, but the gap will not close.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the capital raise needed when leverage is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory CRAR of 18.85% (against 15% minimum and 18% comfort level) is well below what a net-worth-to-AUM view implies; the gap is about Rs 9,000 crore. The enabling resolution keeps Tier 2 and other instruments open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the early-bucket stress in IT-sector salaried loans, and is it flowing to later buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: Early bounce rates are up, not 90+ delinquencies; no flow to later buckets yet. Underwriting was tightened on the margin.

risks_watch: IT-sector salaried stress in South India, mainly secured products; early bounce rates rising, with flow to later buckets to be tracked.
LAP 90+ DPD small sequential uptick; four idiosyncratic cases cited; July trend to be watched.
Wholesale prepayments continue to reduce the book and growth.
Partnerships/digital volumes are cyclical and dependent on Fintech activity; the company says it will scale back if risk rises.
PCR rose on higher ECL assumptions and provision floors; management says PCR is not a target.
544597|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and the FY27 RoAUM path, but cautious on IT-sector salaried stress, which management repeatedly said is too early to call. Management was evasive on the NIM sequential move (attributed mainly to day count and fewer DA sell-downs) and on PCR, saying it is an output of model choices.
key_quotes: In Q1, we choose to reduce our DA sell-down and that mostly explained this slight moderation of NIM.
PCR is not a metric that one targets. PCR is an output, not an input to our decision-making.

rows.why: Gold loan branches rising from 67 to 200 by March 2027 (phase two launched) and net 79 branches added in Q1 to 780 total, so branch network build-out is under way and guided.

rows.why: Retail disbursements grew 44% YoY in Q1 (vs 34% in Q4 FY26) and Retail AUM rose 32% to Rs 91,249 crore, while Wholesale disbursed Rs 2,604 crore, though prepayments limit net book growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital is a constraint but managed via DTA utilisation and investment sell-downs; no new capex plan is announced, and the Rs 4,000 crore raise is an enabling resolution with timing open and CRAR at 18.85% vs 15% minimum.

rows.why: Management reiterated original FY27 guidance on AUM growth, profit growth and RoAUM rather than raising it; Growth PBT rose to Rs 470 crore from Rs 294 crore (+60%) and Growth RoAUM is 1.9%, so an upgrade depends on the path to 2.5% by Q4.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: IT-sector salaried stress is early (bounce rates rising, no flow to later buckets yet), LAP 90+ DPD ticked up, and wholesale prepayments are high (74% of disbursements repaid), all of which could pressure the RoAUM path from 1.9% to 2.5%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launches were discussed beyond gold loan network expansion and PL branch penetration to 100% within two to three quarters.

rows.label: Capital raise up to Rs 4,000 crore

rows.label: Cost of funds and yield stability
rows.why: Cost of borrowing 8.80% (down 4 bps QoQ) and loan yields stable at 13.2-13.4%, but management says the disbursement-to-AUM yield gap will not close, so AUM yield stays structurally below disbursement yield.

rows.label: Digital/partnership volumes tied to Fintech and FLDG
rows.why: Partnership/digital volumes are rising with over 80% under FLDG, but management says it will cut volumes if risk rises, so growth here is conditional on asset quality.

544597|2026-09.headline: Piramal Finance Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 67% YoY to INR545 crores; Growth AUM up 30% YoY and RoAUM 2% annualised.
544597|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 PAT of INR545 crores (up 67% YoY) and H1 PAT above INR1,000 crores, with Growth business PBT at INR538 crores. Total AUM grew 24% YoY to INR1,13,112 crores, with Growth AUM up 30% and the legacy book down 69% YoY to INR1,673 crores. Cost to income improved to 52%, and the company raised INR3,850 crores of equity (QIP INR2,100 crores plus INR1,750 crores promoter warrants). Management reiterated FY27 profit growth guidance of around 50% and a 2.5% exit RoAUM for Q4 FY27, and flagged a possible insurance commission headwind from IRDAI's draft proposal.

FY27 profit growth guidance of about 50% YoY reiterated; management says it is confident of meeting it.
Exit Q4 FY27 Growth RoAUM target of about 2.5% reiterated, even if cost of borrowing does not fall further; management expects further opex reduction of 30-35 bps over the next 6 quarters.

Gold loans are a high-yield product that management is growing, partly at the expense of low-yield mortgages.
Non-dilutive regulatory capital release possible over the next 12 to 24 months; management says this plus the QIP gives runway for growth capital for some years.
Capital raise in Q2 structured to limit leverage hit; QIP added ~200 bps to CAR and 5 bps to RoAUM.
demand_pricing: Disbursements up 34% YoY in Q2, with momentum stronger than Q1.
Unsecured AUM mix at 21% (20% two quarters ago); target 25-26% over coming years. Cross-sell share of unsecured disbursements at 30%.
Mass-affluent housing loans and larger-ticket LAP showing higher growth after rating upgrade.

Incremental borrowing cost: 9.36% (H1 FY26), 8.67% (H2 FY26), 8.46% (H1 FY27). Retiring debt about 9.1% vs new borrowing about 8.4%. About INR37,500 crores of long-term borrowings mature in next 18 months (about INR29,000 crores next year per analyst).

Pricing: NBFC lending rates move with PLR; management said it will not pass on rate increases until its own cost of borrowing rises, with roughly a one-year lag and a further three-month lag to customers.
Market-linked borrowings under one-third of total; almost no repo-linked debt. Q2 raised almost nothing from capital markets, shifting mix to MCLR-linked funding.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will pass on higher rates to customers, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through follows PLR changes, which lag cost of borrowing by about one year; management expects no pass-through yet. Around 50% of assets (HL and LAP) are the main repricing book.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields rise as the legacy book runs off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. Q2 had one extra day, which cut retail yield by about 11 bps; management called this optical. Growth NIM should converge towards company NIM as legacy runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Is the housing loan vintage uptick real?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, driven largely by one INR4 crore fraud case from Q2 FY26; management expects it to fall in Q3. Concentration in South India IT-sector home loans persists but has not spread.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan exposure and risk strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry data shows 15-23% of gross gold disbursements went to customers 90+ days past due. Piramal's October gold disbursements to such customers are under 1%, and it will not disburse to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated provisioning lower than Growth credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy book write-backs (about INR90 crores profit from recovery) offset Growth credit cost, which is used to build other buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Path from 2% to 3% RoAUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex 30-35 bps further reduction over 6 quarters, funding cost reduction and mix shift to unsecured and gold; exit FY27 target 2.5%. FY28 outlook recalibrated for insurance headwind.

qa_highlights.question: How much RoAUM headwind from the insurance commission rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM impact if the IRDAI draft is implemented from 1 April 2027; partly offset by Pramerica Life profit share and sales-incentive rationalisation. Management says mitigating half would still be meaningful.

qa_highlights.question: Does the rising rate cycle hurt NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says rate-cycle positioning is favourable: variable-rate assets INR56,000 crores exceed variable-rate liabilities INR51,000 crores; spreads down 40-45 bps; retiring debt about 60 bps above current borrowing rates.

Wholesale growth headwind from high prepayments (72% of disbursements repaid in Q2).
Housing loan 90+ uptick (one fraud case) and IT-sector delinquencies in South India; management expects Q3 improvement.

544599|2026-03.headline: Studds Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 167.5 crore; FY27 guidance is 17-18% revenue growth with broadly flat EBITDA margin.
544599|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 167.5 crore (up 11.9% YoY), EBITDA INR 31.3 crore (up 11% YoY, margin 18.7%) and PAT INR 21.1 crore (up 6.1% YoY, margin 12.6%). For FY26, revenue was INR 634.2 crore (up 8.6%), EBITDA INR 122.2 crore (up 16.4%, margin 19.3%) and PAT INR 82.7 crore (up 18.7%). Management took 8-9% price increases from 1 April 2026 to offset raw material inflation, but expects Q1 FY27 gross margin pressure before recovery. Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 two-wheeler helmet and boxes volume

financial_highlights.value: INR 3 per share on INR 5 face value (60% payout)

segments.name: STUDDS (domestic mass/core brand)
segments.commentary: Volume grew from 68.7 lakh units in FY24 to 72.6 lakh units in FY26, about 3% CAGR. Management positions it as the scale and stability base.

segments.name: Private label
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 22% CAGR. The largest white label, O'Neal, saw ASP rise from INR 1,831 to INR 1,918.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 20% of FY26 revenue versus 16.75% in FY25, and 22.79% in Q4 versus 17% in Q3. Management guides exports to grow 23-24% in FY27 and reach about 30% of revenue in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 17-18%, with EBITDA margins at broadly similar levels to FY26.
Q1 FY27 gross margin expected under pressure from raw material costs; margins to recover in subsequent quarters as material prices ease.

Management does not expect EBITDA margin to reach 22-23% in FY27; it expects that level only after revenue crosses INR 750 crore with operating leverage, and 12 months out margins should be better than FY26.
Advertising and marketing budget for FY27 set at INR 30 crore, across domestic and export, versus about INR 23 crore in FY26.
Normalised inventory days guided at 85-90, versus 91 days currently and 68 days in the prior year.
Expected 2-3 years of 8-9% price increases; a further 2-2.5% or 3-4% increase is possible if raw material costs stay elevated.

Capacity: installed capacity rises from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units (about 33%), with the first 1.5 million units by Q2 FY27 and the second 1.5 million over the following 15-18 months.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 1.5 million units targeted by Q2 FY27, with a second 1.5 million units expected over the following 15-18 months; total installed capacity to rise from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units.
Capacity utilisation FY26: two-wheeler helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 88%, water decals 57%. Q4 FY26 utilisation: helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 91%, water decals 57%.
Capacity figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix; unpainted-heavy mix raises effective capacity.
Italy subsidiary being incorporated, with a warehouse in Reggio Emilia via a third-party 3PL. Initial stock of 10,000-15,000 units, about three months' cover, with sales expected from mid-Q2 FY27.
Additional warehouse added in Faridabad in FY26.
Riding jackets and an external Bluetooth communication system for helmets are in advanced prototype; commercial sales expected from H2 FY27.
FY26 capex INR 48 crore.
demand_pricing: Price increases averaging 8-9% across the portfolio and channels from 1 April 2026, with export price increases of about 9-10%. Management says the 8-9% offsets current material costs but not full-year costs if they stay at peak levels.
Raw material prices rose after March and have eased in the last two weeks; management says they remain about 20-25% above the pre-spike level and expects about 2-3 months to return to Nov-Dec levels.
Management reports no volume or demand pressure after the April price increase, and says dealers expected a larger increase.
Unorganised share of the Indian helmet market is estimated at 25-30% (not less than 20%), expected to fall to 10-15% over 2-3 years.
Europe: Italy is the focus market, to be served dealer-direct. Mexico: a 1,200-store retail chain signed; Mexico helmet market about 2.5 million units, with the company below 1% share.
Competition: management says unorganised players may exit under price pressure, and many brands, including Chinese OEM suppliers, have raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12 million capacity target conservative if unpainted helmets are produced more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is fungible. The 12 million figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix, and capacity rises if the unpainted share increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and will 8-9% price increases offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8-9% almost offsets current material prices, but not if costs stay at peak. Q1 FY27 margins will be under pressure, and recovery is expected once material prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach 22% as revenue crosses INR 750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not in FY27 because of Q1 raw material pressure. Operating leverage is expected to lift margins above FY26 levels 12 months out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between SMK and STUDDS, and between export and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: SMK EBITDA is about 10 points higher than STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%). Export and domestic margins are roughly similar, with exports mostly SMK, and a gap of about 10 points is cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the European subsidiary moved from Spain to Italy?
qa_highlights.answer: The Spanish distributor objected to a direct subsidiary there. Italy has no direct importer, is the largest European market, and is served by a Dutch distributor with small volumes. The warehouse will be in Reggio Emilia.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise from 68 to 91?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the new Faridabad warehouse and higher US inventory with rising US sales. It says 85-90 days is the comfortable range.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: prices spiked to about 150 (index) before easing to 120-125, and Q1 FY27 gross margin is expected to be under pressure.
Working capital: inventory days rose to 91 from 68, and management targets 85-90 days.
Start-up costs and margin drag from the Italy subsidiary and the Europe 3PL warehouse, and new export markets with their own homologation rules (Brazil, Indonesia, Sri Lanka).
Execution on the Decathlon non-motorised helmet supplies from July 2026 and on the 1.5 million unit capacity addition by Q2 FY27.

Cost initiatives: AI/agentic automation, offshoring to lower-cost geographies, single global system for finance, HR and operations.
Management said no further acquisitions needed near term; growth to come organically by hiring teams for new products and markets.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q1 was about half market growth and half market outperformance, per management.
Middle East conflict has depressed volumes for about 5 to 6 months; inventory corrections drove momentum on transatlantic, transpacific and intra-Asia lanes.
Carrier capacity constrained by disruptions, keeping freight rates elevated; management said freight rates rose about 20% to 30% (per analyst question) and is passed through in revenue and costs.
Gross profit growth of about 6.6% QoQ versus about 4.1% implied by volume mix; management attributed the extra 2 to 2.5% to freight environment and efficiencies.
Industry volumes down about 13% to 14% over last two years; Allcargo outperforming by about 3% to 4%. Growth in Latin America, Southeast Asia and India offset declines in Europe and US.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry cyclical and why have yields fallen since FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the post-COVID 21 to 24 month period was exceptional for FCL margins, and excluding it yield has improved continuously; volumes, not yields, have been the drag. It described the business as shadowing trade conditions rather than cycling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are volumes declining when global trade is broadly flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCL has declined more than the industry on a YoY basis, while FCL decline is higher for Allcargo due to Middle East exposure. No alternative to LCL exists except air for small shipments averaging 3 to 4 cubic metres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost base and is it flat in USD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms; about 80 to 85% of business sits outside India and ocean freight is the largest cost in USD. Rupee translation affects both revenue and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt composition and net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is mainly working capital plus acquisition funding. Consolidated gross debt about INR942 crores and net debt about INR570 crores at June quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and ROCE normalisation path is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA margin guidance, since margins are not a relevant metric in this business. Management said ROCE was historically above 20% and should return there broadly; a 12% to 15% volume increase from current levels is the ballpark needed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, no; management said the strategy is to grow by investing in people rather than buying businesses, as all key markets and products are already covered.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict continuing to depress FCL volumes, particularly in and out of the region, with knock-on impact on North Asia.
LCL volumes still about 4% below last year and about 10% below two years ago; no guidance for substantial growth.
Rupee translation and USD cost base: management intends flat USD cost, but reported INR figures will move with exchange rate.
Net debt reduction targeted over two to three quarters depends on working capital release and divestments; still to be evidenced.
Company does not provide gross or EBITDA margin guidance; a monthly yield trend update (indexed, not absolute) is promised from this month.
PAT still negative (loss of INR28 crores); profitability relies on volume recovery and cost discipline.
544602|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on demand, confident on controllable cost and yield levers. Management repeatedly declined to give margin, ROCE or volume-growth guidance, and framed near-term growth as marginal, while stressing trade-recovery upside and cost discipline.
key_quotes: So at least in the near term, the strategy is to grow by investing in people and not buying businesses.
the business has actually, you know, generated cash in the recent times.
In our business, gross margin honestly does not hold any significant value because gross margin means your profit in percentage terms.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides only marginal incremental profit improvement with yield held flat, and EBITDA swung to INR33 crores from a INR31 crore loss a year ago, but it gives no margin guidance and says volume recovery and cost discipline are needed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Business is asset-light with minimal owned capital assets, capex is a tiny fraction of P&L, and management said no acquisitions are needed; non-core warehousing and office assets worth USD10-15 million are being divested instead.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Base case assumes no substantial volume growth, only a marginal monthly uptick; LCL is down 4% YoY and FCL down double digits, and 12-15% volume growth from current levels is needed for target profitability, which is conditional on market share gains and a trade rebound.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is a tiny fraction of P&L with no utilisation-driven expansion case, and management is focused on divestments and network optimisation rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give margin, ROCE or volume-growth guidance and framed near-term growth as marginal, so no guidance raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East conflict has depressed volumes for 5-6 months, FCL is down double digits YoY, PAT is still a loss of INR28 crores, and net debt reduction depends on working capital release and divestments not yet evidenced.

rows.label: Net debt cut via working capital and non-core divestments
rows.why: Management guided net debt down significantly over 2-3 quarters from about INR570 crores (gross debt about INR942 crores), with USD10-15 million of warehousing and office asset sales, though this is still to be evidenced.

rows.label: Flat USD cost base and AI/offshoring initiatives
rows.why: Management intends to hold employee and admin costs flat in USD terms, and about 80-85% of the business sits outside India, so USD cost discipline is a stated lever.

rows.label: Yield held at current levels with monthly yield trend update
rows.why: Gross profit per unit is expected to hold at current levels and freight rates rose 20-30%, passed through in revenue and costs, while a monthly indexed yield update is promised from this month.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost discipline, yield and net debt reduction, but cautious on demand and declined to give margin, ROCE or volume guidance; analysts pressed on why volumes are falling while global trade is flat and on the cyclical yield decline since FY24.
